title.zh: 卷一百九十 列傳第七十七: 儒學二
title.raw: 卷一百九十 列傳第七十七: 儒學二 Volume 190 Biographies 77: Confucian Scholars 2

sentences.zh: 列傳第七十七 儒學二

translations.literal: Biography 77: Confucian Scholars 2
translations.idiomatic: Biography 77: Confucian Scholars, Part Two

sentences.zh: 胡長孺，字汲仲，婺州永康人。

translations.literal: Hu Changru, style name Jizhong, was a native of Yongkang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Changru, whose style was Jizhong, came from Yongkang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 當唐之季，其先自天台來徙。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tang, his ancestors migrated from Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Tang, his forebears had moved from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 宋南渡後，以進士科發身者十人，持節分符，先後相望。

translations.literal: After the Song crossed south, ten men of the family rose through the jinshi examinations; they held imperial commissions and seals, one after another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song court fled south, ten members of the clan entered official life through the jinshi degree, and for generations they held imperial commissions in office, one following another.

sentences.zh: 曾祖襜，欽州司法參軍，脫略豪雋，輕貲急施，人以鄭莊稱之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chan was a judicial aide in Qinzhou; unrestrained and bold, he treated wealth lightly and gave urgently in charity, and people compared him to Zheng Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chan served as judicial aide in Qinzhou—a man of bold, unconstrained spirit who cared little for money and gave freely in haste; people likened him to Zheng Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 祖岩，起嘉定甲戌進士，知福州閩縣事，卓行危論，奇文瑰句，端平、嘉定間，士大夫皆自以為不可及。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan rose as a jinshi in the jiaxu year of the Jiading reign, became magistrate of Min County in Fuzhou, had outstanding conduct and daring discourse, and wrote marvelous essays and splendid lines; in the Duanping and Jiading periods, scholar-officials all regarded themselves as unable to match him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan passed the jinshi examination in the jiaxu year of Jiading and governed Min County in Fuzhou. His conduct was eminent, his opinions fearless, and his prose studded with striking passages; throughout the Duanping and Jiading eras, the literati considered him beyond their reach.

sentences.zh: 其在江西幕府，平贛州之難於指顧之頃，全活數十萬人。

translations.literal: When he was in the Jiangxi staff headquarters, he settled the crisis at Ganzhou in the turn of a glance and preserved the lives of several hundred thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: While serving on the Jiangxi staff, he quelled the turmoil at Ganzhou almost at a gesture and saved the lives of hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 父居仁，淳祐丁未進士，知台州軍州事，文辭政事，亦絕出於四方。

translations.literal: His father Juren was a jinshi in the dingwei year of Chunyou, became prefect of Taizhou, and in literary composition and administration likewise stood far above others everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juren took the jinshi degree in the dingwei year of Chunyou and served as prefect of Taizhou; in both letters and governance he stood unrivaled across the realm.

sentences.zh: 至長孺，其學益大振，《九經》、諸史，下逮百氏，名、墨、縱橫，旁行敷落，律令章程，無不包羅而揆序之。

translations.literal: By the time of Changru, his learning flourished all the more greatly: the Nine Classics and the various histories, down to the hundred schools, Mohists and Legalists and coalition strategists, running alongside in profusion, statutes and regulations and ordinances—none were not embraced and arranged in order.
translations.idiomatic: In Changru's generation learning reached its height. He mastered the Nine Classics and every history, then ranged through the hundred schools—Mohist, Legalist, coalitionist, and more—along with statutes, regulations, and administrative codes, organizing the whole into a coherent order.

sentences.zh: 咸淳中，外舅徐道隆為荊湖四川宣撫參議官，長孺從之入蜀，銓試第一名，授迪功郎、監重慶府酒務。

translations.literal: In the Xianchun period, his father-in-law Xu Daolong was a staff adviser to the Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu, Sichuan; Changru followed him into Shu, ranked first in the selection examination, and was appointed Diligent Merit Gentleman and supervisor of the Chongqing prefectural wine monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianchun his father-in-law Xu Daolong served as staff adviser to the Pacification Commissioner for Jinghu and Sichuan; Changru accompanied him into Shu, placed first in the qualifying examination, and received appointment as Diligent Merit Gentleman and supervisor of the Chongqing wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 俄用制置使硃孫之辟，兼總領湖廣軍馬錢糧所僉，與高彭、李湜、梅應春等，號南中八士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned by the Pacification Commissioner Zhu Sun's grandson and concurrently served as an aide at the General Office for Military Funds and Grain in Huguang; together with Gao Peng, Li Shen, Mei Yingchun, and others, they were styled the Eight Scholars of the South.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered service under the Pacification Commissioner Zhu Sun's grandson as concurrent aide at the General Office for Military Funds and Grain in Huguang. He and Gao Peng, Li Shen, Mei Yingchun, and others were known as the Eight Scholars of the South.

sentences.zh: 已而復拜福寧州倅之命，會宋亡，退棲永康山中。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again received appointment as deputy prefect of Funing, but when the Song fell he withdrew to dwell in seclusion in the mountains of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed deputy prefect of Funing, but when the Song dynasty collapsed he retired to live in seclusion in the Yongkang hills.

sentences.zh: 至元二十五年，詔下求賢，有司強起之，至京師，待詔集賢院。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Zhiyuan an edict went forth seeking the worthy; the authorities forcibly raised him up; he reached the capital and awaited edicts at the Hall of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Zhiyuan the court issued an edict calling for men of talent, and the authorities pressed him into service. He came to the capital and waited at the Hall of Gathered Talents for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 既而召見內殿，拜集賢修撰，與宰相議不合，改教授揚州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned to audience in the inner hall, appointed Compiler at the Hall of Gathered Talents, disagreed with the chief minister in counsel, and was transferred to serve as instructor at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the inner palace, appointed Compiler at the Hall of Gathered Talents, but when his views clashed with the chief minister's he was reassigned as instructor at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，移建昌，適錄事闕官，檄長孺攝之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was transferred to Jianchang; it happened that the registrar's post was vacant, and an order was issued for Changru to act in the office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was posted to Jianchang, where the registrar's post happened to be vacant; Changru was ordered to fill it on an acting basis.

sentences.zh: 程文海方貴顯，其家氣焰薰灼，即違法，人不敢呵問，其樹外門，侵官道，長孺亟命撤之。

translations.literal: Cheng Wenhai was then noble and prominent; his family's arrogance blazed hot—even when they violated the law no one dared rebuke them. They planted trees outside their gate encroaching on the official road, and Changru urgently ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wenhai was then at the height of power, and his household's arrogance was so fierce that even when they broke the law no one dared challenge them. They had planted trees outside their gate that blocked the official roadway, and Changru promptly ordered them torn down.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，轉台州路寧海縣主簿，階將仕佐郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was transferred to chief clerk of Ninghai County in Taizhou Circuit, with rank Assistant Gentleman for Attending Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida he became chief clerk of Ninghai County in Taizhou Circuit, holding the rank of Assistant Gentleman for Attending Service.

sentences.zh: 大德丁未，浙東大昆，戊申，复無麥，民相枕死。

translations.literal: In the dingwei year of Dade there was a great locust plague in eastern Zhejiang; in the wushen year wheat failed again, and the people died lying one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingwei year of Dade eastern Zhejiang suffered a devastating locust plague; the following wushen year brought another crop failure, and people died in heaps where they lay.

sentences.zh: 宣慰同知脫歡察議行賑荒之令，斂富人錢一百五十萬給之，至縣，以餘錢二十五萬屬長孺藏去，乃行旁州。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner and Associate Administrator Tuohuancha deliberated on carrying out famine-relief orders, collected 1.5 million in cash from the wealthy to distribute, reached the county, entrusted the remaining 250,000 to Changru to store away, and then proceeded to neighboring prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commissioner Tuohuancha set famine relief in motion, collecting 1.5 million cash from the wealthy for distribution. When he reached the county he left 250,000 of the surplus with Changru to hold in storage, then continued on to neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 長孺察其有乾沒意，悉散於民。

translations.literal: Changru perceived that he intended to embezzle it and distributed the whole sum to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Changru saw that Tuohuancha meant to skim the funds and distributed the entire sum to the people.

sentences.zh: 閱月再至，索其錢，長孺抱成案進曰：「錢在是矣。」

translations.literal: After a month he came again and demanded the money; Changru embraced the completed dossier and advanced, saying, "The money is here."
translations.idiomatic: A month later Tuohuancha returned and demanded the money. Changru came forward bearing a completed dossier and said, "Here is your money."

sentences.zh: 脫歡察怒曰：「汝膽如山耶！

translations.literal: Tuohuancha said in anger, "Your courage is like a mountain!
translations.idiomatic: Tuohuancha raged, "Your nerve is as big as a mountain!

sentences.zh: 何所受命，而敢無忌若此！」

translations.literal: From whom do you receive orders, that you dare to be so unrestrained!"
translations.idiomatic: Who authorized you to act with such reckless impunity!"

sentences.zh: 長孺曰：「民一日不食，當有死者，誠不及以聞，然官書具在，可徵也。」

translations.literal: Changru said, "If the people go one day without food, there will be deaths; it is true I did not reach you in time to report, yet the official documents are all in place and can be verified."
translations.idiomatic: Changru replied, "When people miss even one day's food, they die. I admit I did not report to you in time, but the official records are complete and can be checked."

sentences.zh: 脫歡察雖怒，不敢問。

translations.literal: Although Tuohuancha was angry, he did not dare pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Furious though he was, Tuohuancha dared press the matter no further.

sentences.zh: 縣有銅岩，惡少年狙伺其間，恆出鈔道，為過客患，官不能禁。

translations.literal: The county had Copper Cliff, where vicious youths lay in wait; they constantly waylaid the road and were a plague to travelers, and the authorities could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: The county had a place called Copper Cliff where ruffians lay in ambush, constantly robbing travelers on the highway—a scourge the authorities could not suppress.

sentences.zh: 長孺偽衣商人服，令蒼頭負貨以從，陰戒騶卒十人躡其後。

translations.literal: Changru disguised himself in a merchant's dress, ordered a servant to carry goods and follow, and secretly instructed ten mounted attendants to trail behind.
translations.idiomatic: Changru dressed as a merchant, had a servant carry goods behind him, and secretly told ten mounted guards to follow at a distance.

sentences.zh: 長孺至，岩中人突出要之，長孺方遜辭以謝，騶卒俄集，皆成擒，俾盡逮其黨置於法，夜行無虞。

translations.literal: When Changru arrived, the men of the cliff burst out to waylay him; Changru was just making humble excuses in thanks when the mounted attendants suddenly gathered; all were seized; he had their whole gang arrested and punished by law, and thereafter night travel was without worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Changru reached the cliff the bandits sprang out to rob him. He was still making polite excuses when his guards suddenly closed in and seized them all. He had the entire gang arrested and punished, and thereafter travelers passed safely even at night.

sentences.zh: 民荷溺器糞田，偶觸軍卒衣，卒抶傷民，且碎器而去，竟不知主名。

translations.literal: A commoner carrying a night-soil bucket to fertilize his fields accidentally touched a soldier's garment; the soldier beat and wounded the man and smashed the vessel and left, and in the end his identity was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: A farmer carrying a night-soil bucket to his fields accidentally brushed a soldier's coat. The soldier beat him, smashed the bucket, and left—and no one knew who he was.

sentences.zh: 民來訴，長孺陽怒其誣，械於市，俾左右潛偵之，向抶者過焉，戟手稱快，執詣所隸，杖而償其器。

translations.literal: The man came to lodge a complaint; Changru feigned anger at his false accusation and had him shackled in the marketplace, ordering his attendants secretly to watch; when the one who had beaten him passed by, he pointed and exclaimed in satisfaction; they seized him and brought him to his unit, flogged him, and made him compensate for the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The farmer came to complain. Changru pretended to be angry at a false accusation and had him shackled in the marketplace while his men watched in secret. When the soldier who had beaten him passed by, he pointed and crowed with satisfaction. They seized the soldier, brought him to his unit, flogged him, and made him pay for the broken bucket.

sentences.zh: 群嫗聚浮屠庵，誦佛書為禳祈，一嫗失其衣，適長孺出鄉，嫗訟之。

translations.literal: A group of old women gathered at a Buddhist nunnery to chant sutras for blessing and prayer; one woman lost her garment; it happened that Changru was going out of the district, and the woman sued before him.
translations.idiomatic: A group of elderly women had gathered at a Buddhist chapel to chant scriptures for blessings. One woman lost her clothes, and as Changru was passing through the countryside she brought the case to him.

sentences.zh: 長孺以牟麥置群嫗合掌中，命繞佛誦書如初，長孺閉目叩齒，作集神狀，且曰：「吾使神監之矣，盜衣者行數周，麥當芽。」

translations.literal: Changru placed sprouting barley in the palms of the old women's joined hands, ordered them to circle the Buddha and chant as before; Changru closed his eyes and clicked his teeth, assuming the posture of summoning spirits, and said, "I have set spirits to watch; the thief of the garment, after walking several rounds, will find the barley sprout."
translations.idiomatic: Changru placed sprouting barley in each woman's cupped palms and told them to circle the Buddha and chant as before. He closed his eyes, clicked his teeth, and assumed the pose of summoning spirits, saying, "I have set spirits to watch. Whoever stole the clothes—after a few circuits the barley will sprout in her hands."

sentences.zh: 一嫗屢開掌視，長孺指縛之，還所竊衣。

translations.literal: One old woman repeatedly opened her palms to look; Changru pointed and had her bound, and returned the stolen garment.
translations.idiomatic: One woman kept opening her palms to peek. Changru pointed her out, had her bound, and returned the stolen clothes.

sentences.zh: 長孺白事帥府歸，吏言有姦事屢問弗伏者，長孺曰：「此易易爾。」

translations.literal: When Changru returned from reporting business at the commandery headquarters, an clerk said there was an adultery case in which repeated questioning had not produced confession; Changru said, "This is very easy."
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the commandery headquarters an clerk told him of an adultery case in which the suspects would not confess despite repeated questioning. Changru said, "That is easily settled."

sentences.zh: 夜伏吏案下，黎明，出姦者訊之，辭愈堅，長孺佯謂令長曰：「頗聞國家有詔，盍迎之。」

translations.literal: At night he lay concealed beneath the clerk's desk; at dawn he brought out the adulterers for questioning; their words grew all the firmer; Changru pretended to say to the magistrate, "I have heard the state has issued an edict—why not go welcome it?"
translations.idiomatic: That night he hid beneath the clerk's desk. At dawn he brought out the suspects for questioning; they grew only more stubborn. Changru pretended to tell the magistrate, "I hear the court has issued an edict—should we not go welcome it?"

sentences.zh: 叱隸卒縛姦者東西楹，空縣而出，庭無一人。

translations.literal: He shouted at the runners to bind the adulterers to the east and west pillars, emptied the county office and went out, and the courtyard had not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered runners to bind the suspects to the east and west pillars, cleared the county hall, and left the courtyard empty.

sentences.zh: 姦者相謂曰：「事至此，死亦無承，行將自解矣。」

translations.literal: The adulterers said to one another, "The affair has come to this—even death will bring no confession; soon we will be released of ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: The suspects whispered to one another, "It has come to this—even if we die we will not confess. They will have to let us go soon."

sentences.zh: 語畢，案下吏嘩而出，姦者驚，咸叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: When the words were finished, the clerk beneath the desk burst out with a clamor; the adulterers were startled and all knocked their heads and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had they spoken than the clerk burst out from beneath the desk. Startled, the suspects all kowtowed and confessed.

sentences.zh: 永嘉民有弟質珠步搖於兄者，贖焉，兄妻愛之，紿以亡於盜，屢訟不獲直，往告長孺，長孺曰：「爾非吾民也。」

translations.literal: A man of Yongjia had a younger brother who pawned a pearl hairpin to his elder brother; he redeemed it, but the elder brother's wife cherished it and deceived them saying it had been lost to thieves; he sued repeatedly without obtaining justice and went to tell Changru; Changru said, "You are not my subject."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia a younger brother had pawned a pearl hairpin to his elder brother and later redeemed it, but the elder brother's wife coveted it and claimed it had been stolen. Repeated lawsuits brought no justice, so the man went to Changru, who said, "You are not one of my people."

sentences.zh: 叱之去。

translations.literal: He shouted at him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him driven away.

sentences.zh: 未幾，治盜，長孺嗾盜誣兄受步搖為贓，逮兄赴官，力辨數弗置，長孺曰：「爾家信有是，何謂誣耶！」

translations.literal: Before long, while handling a theft case, Changru instructed the thief to accuse the elder brother of receiving the hairpin as stolen goods; the elder brother was seized and brought to court; he argued forcefully several times without release; Changru said, "Your household truly has such a thing—how can you call it false accusation!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long, while prosecuting a theft case, Changru had the thief accuse the elder brother of possessing the hairpin as stolen goods. The brother was arrested and protested repeatedly in vain. Changru said, "Your household really does have such a thing—how can you call this a false charge!"

sentences.zh: 兄倉皇曰：「有固有之，乃弟所質者。」

translations.literal: The elder brother said in panic, "It exists, it exists—it was what the younger brother pawned."
translations.idiomatic: The brother blurted out in panic, "We do have it—it was what my younger brother pawned."

sentences.zh: 趣持至驗之，呼其弟示曰：「得非爾家物乎？」

translations.literal: He hurried to have it brought for verification, summoned the younger brother and showed it, saying, "Is this not your household's object?"
translations.idiomatic: He had it brought at once for inspection, summoned the younger brother, and said, "Is this not your family's property?"

sentences.zh: 弟曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The younger brother said, "It is."
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother said, "It is."

sentences.zh: 遂歸焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was returned.
translations.idiomatic: And so it was restored to him.

sentences.zh: 其行事多類此，不能盡載。

translations.literal: His conduct in office was mostly of this kind and cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his official conduct was of this sort, and not all of it can be recorded here.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，轉兩浙都轉運鹽使司長山場鹽司丞，階將仕郎，未上，以病辭，不復仕，隱杭之虎林山以終。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was transferred to Salt Commissioner of Changshan Field under the Zhejiang Salt Transport Commission, with rank Gentleman for Attending Service; he did not take up the post, resigned on grounds of illness, never again served in office, and lived in seclusion on Tiger Grove Mountain in Hangzhou until his end.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed Salt Commissioner of Changshan Field under the Zhejiang Salt Transport Commission with the rank of Gentleman for Attending Service, but he never took office, resigned citing illness, and never served again, ending his days in seclusion on Tiger Grove Mountain near Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長孺初師青田餘學古，學古師王夢松，夢松亦青田人，傳龍泉葉味道之學，味道則硃熹弟子也。

translations.literal: Changru at first studied under Yu Xuegu of Qingtian; Xuegu studied under Wang Mengsong; Mengsong was also from Qingtian and transmitted the learning of Ye Weidao of Longquan; Weidao was a disciple of Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Changru first studied under Yu Xuegu of Qingtian, who had studied under Wang Mengsong—also of Qingtian and heir to the learning of Ye Weidao of Longquan, a disciple of Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 淵源既正，長孺益行四方，訪求其旨趣，始信涵養用敬為最切，默存靜觀，超然自得，故其為人，光明宏偉，專務明本心之學，慨然以孟子自許。

translations.literal: Since the source stream was already correct, Changru all the more traveled the four quarters seeking its purport; he came to believe that nurturing oneself through reverence was most essential; silently preserving and quietly observing, he transcended and attained for himself; therefore as a man he was bright and grand, devoted solely to illuminating the learning of the original mind, and boldly took Mencius as his measure.
translations.idiomatic: With so orthodox a lineage, Changru traveled widely to pursue its meaning and came to believe that self-cultivation through reverence was paramount. Through silent preservation and quiet observation he attained a transcendent self-possession. As a man he was luminous and magnanimous, devoted to illuminating the original mind, and boldly measured himself against Mencius.

sentences.zh: 唯恐斯道之失其傳，誘引不倦，一時學者慕之，有如飢渴之於食飲。

translations.literal: He feared only that this Way might lose its transmission; he guided and drew others without weariness; scholars of the time admired him as hunger and thirst admire food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing only that the Way might cease to be transmitted, he taught without tiring, and scholars of the day flocked to him as the hungry and thirsty flock to food and drink.

sentences.zh: 方嶽大臣與郡二千石，聘致庠序，敷繹經義，環聽者數百人。

translations.literal: Regional ministers and prefectural administrators of two thousand dan invited him to the schools, where he expounded the classics' meaning; those seated around listening numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors and prefects invited him to lecture in the schools, where he expounded the classics to audiences of several hundred seated around him.

sentences.zh: 長孺為言：「人雖最靈，與物同產，初無二本。」

translations.literal: Changru said in address, "Though man is most spiritually keen, he is produced together with things and from the first has no second root."
translations.idiomatic: Changru declared, "Though humanity is the most spiritually keen of beings, we arise from the same source as all things and were never divided into two natures."

sentences.zh: 皆躍躍然興起，至有太息者。

translations.literal: All leapt up in excitement, and some even sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: All were stirred to excitement, and some sighed with deep emotion.

sentences.zh: 為辭章有精魄，金舂玉撞，壹發其和平之音，海內來求者，如購拱璧，碑版焜煌，照耀四裔，苟非其人，雖一金易一字，毅然不與。

translations.literal: In literary composition he had vital spirit; like gold pounded and jade struck, with one release of his harmonious tone, those who came seeking from within the seas were like purchasing a round jade disk; his stele inscriptions blazed splendid, illuminating the four borderlands; if the person were not right, even for one cash to change one character he firmly would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: His literary compositions had soul and force, like gold hammered and jade struck—one touch and their harmonious tone rang out. Seekers came from across the realm as if buying a sacred jade disk. His commemorative inscriptions blazed with splendor and lit the four quarters, yet if the patron was unworthy he would not sell a single character for any price.

sentences.zh: 鄉闈取士，屢司文衡，貴實賤華，文風為之一變。

translations.literal: In provincial examinations for selecting scholars he repeatedly presided over the literary balance; he valued substance and disdained ornament, and the literary current was thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served as chief examiner in provincial competitions, prizing substance over ornament and thereby transforming the literary climate.

sentences.zh: 晚寓武林，病喘上氣者頗久。

translations.literal: In his later years he lodged at Wulin, afflicted with asthmatic panting and upward qi for quite a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he lived at Wulin, suffering for a long time from asthma and labored breathing.

sentences.zh: 一旦具酒食，與比鄰別，雲將返故鄉，門人有識其微意者，問曰：「先生精神不衰，何為遽欲觀化乎？」

translations.literal: One day he prepared wine and food and took leave of his neighbors, saying he would return to his native place; a disciple who grasped his subtle meaning asked, "Master, your spirit is not declining—why do you so hastily wish to observe transformation?"
translations.idiomatic: One day he prepared wine and food and bade his neighbors farewell, saying he would return to his native place. A disciple who sensed his meaning asked, "Master, your spirit is undiminished—why do you so suddenly speak of departing this life?"

sentences.zh: 長孺曰：「精神與死生，初無相涉也。」

translations.literal: Changru said, "Spirit and death and life from the first have nothing to do with each other."
translations.idiomatic: Changru replied, "Spirit and life and death were never connected in the first place."

sentences.zh: 就寢，至夜半，喘忽止，其子駒排戶視之，則正衣冠坐逝矣。

translations.literal: He went to bed; by midnight the panting suddenly ceased; his son Ju pushed open the door to look and found him sitting in correct cap and robes, having passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to bed. At midnight his breathing suddenly stopped. His son Ju opened the door and found him seated in proper cap and robes, already departed.

sentences.zh: 年七十五。

translations.literal: His age was seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-five years old.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《瓦缶編》、《南昌集》、《寧海漫抄》、《顏樂齋稿》行於世。

translations.literal: Books he authored that circulated in the world include Collected Earthenware Vessels, Nanchang Collection, Ninghai Miscellany, and Drafts from the Studio of Delight in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His works in circulation included Collected Earthenware Vessels, Nanchang Collection, Ninghai Miscellany, and Drafts from the Studio of Delight in Yan.

sentences.zh: 其從兄之綱、之純，皆以經術文學名。

translations.literal: His cousins Zhigang and Zhichun were both renowned for classical learning and literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins Zhigang and Zhichun were both celebrated for classical learning and letters.

sentences.zh: 之綱字仍仲，嘗被薦書。

translations.literal: Zhigang's style name was Yizhong; he once received a recommendation memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigang, style Yizhong, had once been recommended in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 其於聲音字畫之說，自言獨造其妙，惜其書不傳。

translations.literal: Regarding theories of sound, writing, and graphs, he said himself that he alone had attained their subtlety; it is a pity his books were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: On phonology and the theory of written graphs he claimed to have reached insights no one else had matched, but regrettably his writings did not survive.

sentences.zh: 之純字穆仲，咸淳甲戌進士，踐履如古獨行者，文尤明潔可誦。

translations.literal: Zhichun's style name was Muzhong; he was a jinshi in the jiaxu year of Xianchun; his conduct was like an ancient solitary walker; his writing was especially clear and clean, fit for recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichun, style Muzhong, passed the jinshi examination in the jiaxu year of Xianchun. He lived like an ancient solitary exemplar, and his prose was especially lucid and polished, a pleasure to recite.

sentences.zh: 人稱之為三胡云。

translations.literal: People called them the Three Hus.
translations.idiomatic: People called them the Three Hus.

sentences.zh: 熊朋來，字與可，豫章人。

translations.literal: Xiong Penglai, style name Yuhe, was a native of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Penglai, whose style was Yuhe, came from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 宋咸淳甲戌，登進士第第四人，授從仕郎、寶慶府僉書判官公事，未上而宋亡。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year of Xianchun of the Song he placed fourth on the jinshi list, was appointed Attendant Gentleman and aide to the Baoqing prefectural judge for administrative affairs, and did not take office before the Song fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year of Xianchun he ranked fourth on the jinshi list and was appointed Attendant Gentleman and aide to the Baoqing prefectural judge, but the Song fell before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 世祖初得江南，盡求宋之遺士而用之，尤重進士，以故相留夢炎為尚書，召甲戌狀元王龍澤為江南行台監察御史。

translations.literal: When Shizu first obtained the Jiangnan region, he sought out all remaining scholars of the Song to employ them, especially valuing jinshi graduates; he therefore made the former chief minister Liu Mengyan Minister, and summoned the jiaxu top graduate Wang Longze as Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai first secured the Jiangnan region he sought out every remaining Song scholar for service, especially favoring jinshi graduates. He appointed the former chief minister Liu Mengyan Minister and summoned the jiaxu top graduate Wang Longze as Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朋來，龍澤榜下進士，而聲名不在龍澤下，然不肯表襮苟進，隱處州里間，生徒受學者，常百數十人。

translations.literal: Penglai was a jinshi of Wang Longze's examination year, yet his reputation was not below Longze's; however, he was unwilling to display himself and advance hastily, and lived in seclusion in his district and village; students receiving his instruction commonly numbered one or two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Penglai had passed the jinshi in Wang Longze's year and enjoyed a reputation no less than Longze's, yet he refused to parade himself for advancement and lived in seclusion in his home district, where students under his instruction commonly numbered well over a hundred.

sentences.zh: 取硃子《小學》書，提其要領以示之，學者家傳其書，幾遍天下。

translations.literal: He took Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning, extracted its essentials to show them, and scholars transmitted his book in every household, nearly covering all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He distilled the essentials of Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning for his students, and households across the realm passed his book from hand to hand until it was known nearly everywhere.

sentences.zh: 豫章為江西會府，行中書省、提刑按察司皆在焉，凡居是官者，多朝廷名公卿，皆以賓禮延見。

translations.literal: Yuzhang was the metropolitan prefecture of Jiangxi; the Branch Secretariat and the Surveillance Commission were both located there; all who held these offices were mostly renowned ministers of the court, and all received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang was the Jiangxi provincial capital, seat of both the Branch Secretariat and the Surveillance Commission. The men who held those posts were mostly eminent court ministers, and all received him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲之子惇為參知政事，以師禮事朋來，終身稱門人。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian's son Dun served as Associate Administrator; he treated Penglai with the ceremony due a teacher and all his life called himself a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian's son Dun, who served as Associate Administrator, treated Penglai with the deference owed a teacher and called himself his disciple for life.

sentences.zh: 劉宣為提刑按察使，尤加禮敬。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan served as Surveillance Commissioner and especially added courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, the Surveillance Commissioner, showed him particular honor.

sentences.zh: 朋來和而不肆，介而不狷，與群賢講論經義無虛日，儒者咸倚以為重焉。

translations.literal: Penglai was harmonious yet not unrestrained, firm yet not narrow; with the assembled worthies he discussed the classics' meaning without an idle day; Confucians all relied on him as a weighty figure.
translations.idiomatic: Penglai was harmonious without being loose, principled without being rigid. He debated the classics daily with fellow scholars, and the Confucian community looked to him as a pillar.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣治書侍御史王構銓外選於江西，於是參政徐琰、李世安列薦朋來為閩海提舉儒學官，使者報聞，而朝廷以東南儒學之士唯福建、廬陵最盛，特起朋來連為兩郡教授。

translations.literal: It happened that the court dispatched Investigating Censor Wang Gou to conduct external selection in Jiangxi; thereupon Associate Administrators Xu Yan and Li Shi'an jointly recommended Penglai as Commissioner for Promoting Confucian Studies in Minhai; the envoy reported approval, and because among southeastern Confucian scholars only Fujian and Luling were most flourishing, the court specially raised Penglai to serve consecutively as instructor in two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent Investigating Censor Wang Gou to conduct external examinations in Jiangxi, Associate Administrators Xu Yan and Li Shi'an jointly recommended Penglai as Commissioner for Promoting Confucian Studies in Minhai. The court, noting that Fujian and Luling boasted the strongest Confucian communities in the southeast, specially appointed him to teach consecutively in two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 所至，考古篆籀文字，調律呂，協歌詩，以興雅樂，制器定辭，必則古式，學者化焉。

translations.literal: Wherever he arrived, he investigated ancient seal and clerical script, tuned pitch pipes, harmonized songs and odes to revive elegant music, fashioned instruments and fixed texts, always taking ancient models as standard, and scholars were transformed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he researched ancient seal and clerical scripts, tuned pitch pipes, harmonized songs and odes to revive court music, fashioned instruments and fixed texts according to ancient models, and transformed the scholars around him.

sentences.zh: 既滿考，以常格調建安縣主簿，不赴。

translations.literal: After his term was complete, by regular regulation he was transferred to chief clerk of Jian'an County, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was routinely transferred to chief clerk of Jian'an County, but he declined to go.

sentences.zh: 晚以福清州判官致仕，朋來視之，漠如也。

translations.literal: In his later years he retired as vice-prefect of Fuqing, but Penglai regarded it with indifference.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he retired as vice-prefect of Fuqing, a title Penglai regarded with complete indifference.

sentences.zh: 四方學者，因其所自號，稱為天慵先生。

translations.literal: Scholars from the four quarters, according to the style name he gave himself, called him Master Tianyong.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere, following the name he chose for himself, called him Master Tianyong.

sentences.zh: 每燕居，鼓瑟而歌以自樂。

translations.literal: Whenever at leisure in repose, he would strum the zither and sing for his own delight.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure hours he would play the zither and sing for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《瑟賦》二篇，學者爭傳誦之。

translations.literal: He once composed two "Rhapsodies on the Zither," which scholars vied to transmit and recite.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote two Rhapsodies on the Zither, which scholars competed to copy and recite.

sentences.zh: 門人歸之者日盛，旁近舍皆滿，至不能容。

translations.literal: Disciples returning to him daily grew abundant; neighboring houses were all full, until they could not contain them.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples flocked to him in ever greater numbers until neighboring houses were full and could hold no more.

sentences.zh: 朋來懇懇為說經旨文義，老益不倦。

translations.literal: Penglai earnestly expounded the classics' purport and literary meaning; in old age he grew all the more untiring.
translations.idiomatic: Penglai lectured earnestly on the meaning of the classics and grew only more tireless with age.

sentences.zh: 得其所指授者，多為聞人。

translations.literal: Those who received his pointed instruction mostly became renowned men.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those who studied under him became celebrated figures.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，詔以進士科取士，時科舉廢已久，有司咸不知其典故，以不稱明詔為懼，行省官主其事者，諮問於朋來，動中軌度，因以申請，四方得遵用之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou an edict ordered selection of scholars through the jinshi examinations; the examinations had long been abolished, and the authorities all did not know their precedents, fearing they would not match the bright edict; the provincial officials in charge of the matter consulted Penglai; his answers all hit the standard measure, and thereby they submitted applications, and the four quarters were able to follow and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanyou the court revived the jinshi examinations after they had been suspended for years. The officials in charge knew none of the old procedures and feared they would fail the imperial mandate. The provincial authorities consulted Penglai, whose answers hit every mark, and on his advice regulations were submitted that the whole realm could follow.

sentences.zh: 及請為考試官，則曰：「應試者十九及吾門，不可。」

translations.literal: When they asked him to serve as examination officer, he said, "Nine-tenths of the candidates have passed through my gate—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When they asked him to serve as chief examiner he refused, saying, "Nine out of ten candidates have studied under me—that will not do."

sentences.zh: 其後江浙、湖廣，皆卑詞緻禮，請為主文，朋來屢往應之。

translations.literal: Thereafter Jiangzhe and Huguang all with humble words and elaborate courtesy asked him to serve as chief examiner; Penglai went repeatedly to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Jiangzhe and Huguang provinces all sent humble, elaborate invitations asking him to serve as chief examiner, and he went repeatedly to oblige them.

sentences.zh: 及對大廷，其所選士居天下三之一焉。

translations.literal: When they faced the great court, the scholars he selected comprised one-third of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination the candidates he had selected accounted for a third of all graduates in the empire.

sentences.zh: 初，朋來以《周禮》首薦鄉郡，而元制，《周官》不與設科，治《戴記》者又鮮，朋來屢以為言。

translations.literal: At first Penglai had been first recommended in his home district on the Rites of Zhou, but under Yuan regulations the Offices of Zhou was not included among examination subjects, and those who studied the Record of the Elder Dai were also few; Penglai repeatedly spoke on this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Penglai had been first recommended in his home district on the Rites of Zhou, but Yuan regulations excluded the Offices of Zhou from the examination curriculum and few scholars studied the Elder Dai's Record of Rites. Penglai raised the issue repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 蓋朋來之學，諸經中《三禮》尤深，是以當世言禮學者，咸推宗之。

translations.literal: For Penglai's learning among the classics was especially deep in the Three Rites; therefore those who spoke of ritual learning in his age all took him as their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Among the classics Penglai's learning ran deepest in the Three Rites, and scholars of ritual studies in his day all looked to him as their authority.

sentences.zh: 至治中，英宗始採用古禮，親禦袞冕祠太廟，銳意於制禮作樂之事，翰林學士元明善，揚言於朝，以朋來為薦，未及召而卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the Zhizhi period Emperor Yingzong first adopted ancient rites, personally donned imperial robes and cap to sacrifice at the Grand Temple, and was keen on matters of instituting rites and composing music; Hanlin Academician Yuan Mingshan spoke openly at court recommending Penglai, but before he could be summoned he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhizhi, Emperor Yingzong began reviving ancient rites, personally wearing full court dress to sacrifice at the Grand Temple and pressing forward with ritual and music reform. Hanlin Academician Yuan Mingshan openly recommended Penglai at court, but before the summons arrived Penglai died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 朋來動止有常，喜怒不形於色，接賓客，人人各自以得其意。

translations.literal: Penglai's movements and stops had regular pattern; joy and anger did not show on his face; when receiving guests, each person individually felt he had obtained his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Penglai's conduct was measured and steady; joy and anger never showed on his face. When receiving guests, each left feeling fully understood.

sentences.zh: 有家集三十卷，其大者明乎禮樂之事，關於世教，其餘若天文、地理、方技、名物、度數，靡不精究。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan; its greater part clarified matters of rites and music relevant to worldly instruction; the rest, such as astronomy, geography, technical arts, named objects, and measures and numbers—none were not meticulously investigated.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty juan, chiefly clarifying ritual and music as they bear on civilizing the world. He also investigated astronomy, geography, technical arts, material culture, and measurement with equal thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 子太古，鄉貢進士。

translations.literal: His son Taigu was a jinshi by provincial recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taigu passed the jinshi examination by provincial recommendation.

sentences.zh: 戴錶元，字帥初，一字曾伯，慶元奉化州人。

translations.literal: Dai Biaoyuan, style name Shuaichu, alternative style Zengbo, was a native of Fenghua Prefecture in Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Biaoyuan, whose style was Shuaichu and who also used the style Zengbo, came from Fenghua in Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 七歲學古詩文，多奇語。

translations.literal: At age seven he studied ancient poetry and prose, with many striking phrases.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he began studying classical poetry and prose, producing many striking lines.

sentences.zh: 稍長，從裡師習詞賦，輒棄不肯為。

translations.literal: When somewhat older, he followed a village teacher in studying rhapsodic composition, but would cast it aside and refuse to write.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he studied rhapsodic composition under a local teacher but soon abandoned it and refused to write in that genre.

sentences.zh: 咸淳中，入太學，以三舍法升內舍生，既而試禮部第十人，登進士乙科，教授建康府。

translations.literal: In the Xianchun period he entered the Imperial Academy, rose by the three-college method to inner-college student, thereafter placed tenth in the Ministry of Rites examination, passed the jinshi second class, and was appointed instructor at Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianchun he entered the Imperial Academy, advanced through the three-college system to inner-college standing, placed tenth in the Ministry of Rites examination, passed the jinshi in the second class, and was appointed instructor at Jiankang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後遷臨安教授，行戶部掌故，皆不就。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to instructor at Lin'an and acting registrar of the Ministry of Revenue, but he took none of these posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was later offered posts as instructor at Lin'an and acting registrar in the Ministry of Revenue, but accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，表元年已六十餘，執政者薦於朝，起家拜信州教授，再調教授婺州，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade, Biaoyuan was already over sixty; those in power recommended him to court; he rose from private life and was appointed instructor at Xinzhou, then transferred to instructor at Wuzhou, and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dade, Biaoyuan was already past sixty. Those in power recommended him at court, and he entered service as instructor at Xinzhou, then at Wuzhou, before resigning citing illness.

sentences.zh: 初，表元閔宋季文章氣萎篸而辭骫蔟，蔟弊已甚，慨然以振起斯文為己任。

translations.literal: At first Biaoyuan grieved that in the late Song literary spirit had withered and language grown servile and clustered; the clustering evil was already extreme, and he boldly took reviving this culture as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Biaoyuan lamented that late-Song writing had lost its vigor and grown servile and mannered—a corruption already deep. He resolved to revive the literary tradition himself.

sentences.zh: 時四明王應麟、天台舒岳祥並以文學師表一代，表元皆從而受業焉。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Yinglin of Siming and Shu Yuexiang of Tiantai were both literary models for a generation, and Biaoyuan studied under both.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yinglin of Siming and Shu Yuexiang of Tiantai were then the leading literary models of their generation, and Biaoyuan studied under both.

sentences.zh: 故其學博而肆，其文清深雅潔，化陳腐為神奇，蓄而始發，間事摹畫，而隅角不露，施於人者多，尤自秘重，不妄許與。

translations.literal: Therefore his learning was broad and expansive; his writing clear, deep, elegant, and clean; he transformed the stale into the marvelous; storing and then releasing; occasionally depicting matters in miniature without showing a corner of artifice; what he bestowed on people was much, yet he especially kept himself secret and weighty, not lightly granting approval.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was broad and free-ranging; his prose clear, deep, and refined. He turned stale writing into something marvelous, holding force in reserve before releasing it. Even when sketching incidental subjects he never showed artifice. He gave generously to others yet guarded his approval and rarely granted it lightly.

sentences.zh: 至元、大德間，東南以文章大家名重一時者，唯表元而已。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan and Dade periods, among those in the southeast famed as great literary houses for a time, only Biaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiyuan and Dade, among the great literary names of the southeast for a generation, only Biaoyuan stood apart.

sentences.zh: 其門人最知名者曰袁桷，桷之文，其體裁議論，一取法於表元者也。

translations.literal: Among his disciples the most renowned was Yuan Que; Que's writing in form and argument wholly took Biaoyuan as its model.
translations.idiomatic: His best-known disciple was Yuan Que, whose forms of composition and argumentative style wholly followed Biaoyuan's model.

sentences.zh: 表元晚年，翰林集賢以修撰、博士二職論薦，而老疾不可起，年六十七卒。

translations.literal: In Biaoyuan's later years the Hanlin Academy and Hall of Gathered Talents discussed recommending him for Compiler and Academician, but old age and illness prevented his rising; he died at sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life the Hanlin Academy and Hall of Gathered Talents considered recommending him as Compiler and Academician, but age and illness kept him from office. He died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 有《剡源集》行於世。

translations.literal: He had the Shanyuan Collection circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Shanyuan Collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 當表元時，有四明任士林者，亦以文章知名云。

translations.literal: In Biaoyuan's time there was also Ren Shilin of Siming, likewise renowned for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: During Biaoyuan's era Ren Shilin of Siming was also celebrated for his writing.

sentences.zh: 牟應龍，字伯成，其先蜀人，後徙居吳興。

translations.literal: Mou Yinglong, style name Bocheng, his ancestors were Shu people who later migrated to live in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Yinglong, style Bocheng, came from Shu; his family later settled in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖子才仕宋，贈光祿大夫，諡清忠。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zicai served the Song and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the posthumous title Pure and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zicai served the Song and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the posthumous title Pure and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 父巘，為大理少卿。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan served as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 應龍幼警敏過人，日記數千言，文章有渾厚之氣。

translations.literal: Yinglong in youth was keen and surpassing others; each day he memorized several thousand words; his writing had a quality of depth and richness.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yinglong was exceptionally quick-witted, memorizing thousands of characters a day, and his writing had a rich, weighty tone.

sentences.zh: 應龍當以世賞補京官，盡讓諸從弟，而擢咸淳進士第。

translations.literal: Yinglong was to enter the capital bureaucracy by hereditary privilege but yielded it entirely to his younger cousins and instead rose through the Xianchun jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was entitled to enter the capital bureaucracy by hereditary privilege but yielded the benefit to his younger cousins and instead passed the jinshi examination in Xianchun.

sentences.zh: 時賈似道當國，自儗伊、周，謂馬廷鸞曰：「君故與清忠遊，其孫幸見之，當處以高第。」

translations.literal: At the time Jia Sidao held the state, comparing himself to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; he said to Ma Tingluan, "You were once friendly with Pure and Loyal; if his grandson is fortunate enough to meet me, he should be placed in the top rank."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao then dominated the government, comparing himself to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. He told Ma Tingluan, "You once knew Pure and Loyal—if his grandson will see me, I shall place him at the top of the list."

sentences.zh: 應龍拒之不見。

translations.literal: Yinglong refused him and would not meet.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong refused and would not see him.

sentences.zh: 及對策，具言上下內外之情不通、國勢危急之狀，考官不敢置上第。

translations.literal: At the policy response he fully stated that feelings between above and below and inside and outside were not communicating and that the state's peril was critical; the examiners did not dare place him in the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the policy examination he laid out how communication had broken down at every level of government and how dire the state's situation had become. The examiners dared not rank him at the top.

sentences.zh: 調光州定城尉，應龍曰：「昔吾祖對策，以直言忤史彌遠，得洪雅尉，今固當爾，無愧也。」

translations.literal: He was assigned as sheriff of Dingcheng in Guang Prefecture; Yinglong said, "In the past my grandfather answered the policy questions and, for blunt speech, offended Shi Miyuan and received the post of sheriff of Hongya; today it should indeed be so—there is no shame."
translations.idiomatic: Assigned sheriff of Dingcheng in Guang Prefecture, he said, "My grandfather once answered the policy questions, offended Shi Miyuan with blunt speech, and received the post of sheriff of Hongya. Today it should be the same—and I feel no shame."

sentences.zh: 沿海制置司辟為屬，以疾辭不仕，而宋亡矣。

translations.literal: The Coastal Pacification Commission summoned him as staff, but he declined on grounds of illness and did not serve, and then the Song fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Coastal Pacification Commission invited him as staff, but he declined citing illness and never served—and then the Song fell.

sentences.zh: 故相留夢炎事世祖，為吏部尚書，以書招之，曰：「苟至，翰林可得也。」

translations.literal: The former chief minister Liu Mengyan served Shizu as Minister of Personnel and wrote to recruit him, saying, "If you come, you may obtain a Hanlin post."
translations.idiomatic: The former chief minister Liu Mengyan, serving Kublai as Minister of Personnel, wrote to recruit him: "Come, and a Hanlin post may be yours."

sentences.zh: 應龍不答。

translations.literal: Yinglong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong did not answer.

sentences.zh: 已而起家教授溧陽州，晚以上元縣主簿致仕。

translations.literal: Thereafter he rose from private life as instructor at Liyang Prefecture, and in his later years retired as chief clerk of Shangyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered service as instructor at Liyang Prefecture and retired in old age as chief clerk of Shangyuan County.

sentences.zh: 初，宋亡時，大理卿已退不任事，一門父子，自為師友，討論經學，以義理相切磨，於諸經皆有成說，惟《五經音考》盛行於世。

translations.literal: At first when the Song fell the Vice Minister of Justice had already retired and held no office; father and son in one household became teacher and student for each other, discussing classical learning and sharpening one another on principle and meaning; they had settled views on all the classics, and only the Phonological Studies of the Five Classics circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fell his father had already retired from the Vice Ministry of Justice. Father and son made a household school, debating the classics and testing one another on principle. They developed settled views on every classic, and only their Phonological Studies of the Five Classics achieved wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 應龍為文，長於敘事，時人求其文者，車轍交於門，以文章大家稱於東南，人儗之為眉山蘇氏父子，而學者因應龍所自號，稱之曰隆山先生。

translations.literal: Yinglong in writing excelled at narrative; those who sought his writing had carriage tracks crossing at his gate; he was called a great literary house in the southeast; people compared him to the father and sons of the Su clan of Meishan; and scholars, from the style name he gave himself, called him Master Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong excelled at narrative writing. Seekers crowded his gate with carriage tracks, and the southeast hailed him as a literary master, comparing him to the Su father and sons of Meishan. Scholars called him Master Longshan after the name he chose for himself.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Taiding, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Taiding at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 鄭滁孫，字景歐，處州人。

translations.literal: Zheng Chusun, style name Jing'ou, was a native of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chusun, style Jing'ou, came from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋景定間，登進士第，知溫州樂清縣，累歷宗正丞、禮部郎官。

translations.literal: In the Jingding period of the Song he passed the jinshi examination, became magistrate of Yueqing County in Wenzhou, and successively served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingding era he passed the jinshi, governed Yueqing County in Wenzhou, and rose through posts including Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 至元三十年，有以滁孫名薦者，世祖召見，授集賢直學士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan someone recommended Chusun by name; Shizu summoned him to audience and appointed him Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan someone recommended him by name. Kublai summoned him and appointed him Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.

sentences.zh: 尋升侍講學士，又升學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Erudite Lecturer, then again to Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Erudite Lecturer and then to Academician.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，歸田裡。

translations.literal: He requested retirement and returned to his fields and village.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 弟陶孫，字景潛，亦登進士第，監西嶽祠。

translations.literal: His younger brother Taosun, style Jingqian, also passed the jinshi examination and served as custodian of the Western Marchmount Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Taosun, style Jingqian, also passed the jinshi and served as custodian of the Western Marchmount Shrine.

sentences.zh: 先，陶孫徵至闕，奏對稱旨，授翰林國史院編修官，會纂修國史至宋德祐末年事，陶孫曰：「臣嘗仕宋，宋是年亡，義不忍書，書之非義矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier Taosun had been summoned to court; his responses at audience matched the ruler's intent; he was appointed Compiler at the Hanlin National History Office; when they came to compile the national history down to the final year of Song Dezuo, Taosun said, "Your subject once served the Song; in that year the Song perished—I cannot bear to write it, for writing it would not be righteous."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taosun had been summoned to court, answered to the emperor's satisfaction, and was appointed Compiler at the Hanlin National History Office. When the compilers reached the final year of Song Dezuo, Taosun said, "I once served the Song. That was the year it perished—I cannot bear to record it, for to write it would be unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 終不書，世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the end he did not write it; Shizu praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He never wrote it, and Kublai praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 升應奉翰林文字，後出為江西儒學提舉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Attendant for Drafting, and later went out as Commissioner for Promoting Confucian Studies in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Attendant for Drafting and later served as Commissioner for Promoting Confucian Studies in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 滁孫兄弟在當時，最號博洽，儒學之士翕然推之。

translations.literal: The Chusun brothers were at the time the most famed for broad learning; Confucian scholars all looked up to them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chusun brothers were then the most celebrated for erudition, and Confucian scholars looked up to them together.

sentences.zh: 隆福宮以其兄弟前朝士，乃製衣親賜，人以為異遇焉。

translations.literal: Longfu Palace, because they were former dynasty scholars, personally made robes and bestowed them—people regarded this as an extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Because they were scholars of the former dynasty, Longfu Palace had robes made and bestowed them personally—an honor people regarded as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 滁孫所著，有《大易法像通贊》、《周易記玩》等書。

translations.literal: What Chusun authored includes Great Changes: Images, General Commentary, and Records of Zhou Yi Study.
translations.idiomatic: Chusun's works included Great Changes: Images, General Commentary and Records of Zhou Yi Study.

sentences.zh: 陶孫有文集若干卷。

translations.literal: Taosun had a collected works in several juan.
translations.idiomatic: Taosun left a collected works in several juan.

sentences.zh: 陳孚，字剛中，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Chen Fu, style name Gangzhong, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu, style Gangzhong, came from Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼清峻穎悟，讀書過目輒成誦，終身不忘。

translations.literal: In youth he was clear, lofty, and quick to understand; what he read he could recite after one look and never forgot all his life.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was sharp and penetrating; what he read once he could recite from memory for life.

sentences.zh: 至元中，孚以布衣上《大一統賦》，江浙行省為轉聞於朝，署上蔡書院山長，考滿，謁選京師。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan period Fu, as a commoner, submitted the "Rhapsody on Great Unity"; the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat forwarded it to court; he was appointed head of Shangcai Academy; when his term was complete he went to the capital for selection.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiyuan he submitted the "Rhapsody on Great Unity" as a commoner. The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat forwarded it to court, and he was appointed head of Shangcai Academy. When his term ended he went to the capital for appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，世祖命梁曾以吏部尚書再使安南，選南士為介，朝臣薦孚博學有氣節，調翰林國史院編修官，攝禮部郎中，為曾副。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Shizu ordered Liang Zeng, again as Minister of Personnel, to go as envoy to Annan; a southerner was chosen as aide; court ministers recommended Fu for broad learning and integrity of spirit; he was transferred to Compiler at the Hanlin National History Office, acting Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, and served as Zeng's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Kublai sent Liang Zeng again as Minister of Personnel to Annan and needed a southern scholar as aide. Ministers recommended Fu for erudition and moral backbone. He was appointed Compiler at the Hanlin National History Office and acting Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites as Zeng's deputy.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，賜五品服，佩金符以行。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he was granted fifth-rank robes and a gold tally to travel.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he received fifth-rank robes and a gold tally for the journey.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，至安南，世子陳日燇以憂制不出郊，遣陪臣來迎，又不由陽明中門入，曾與孚回館，致書詰日燇以不庭之罪，且責日燇當出郊迎詔，及講新朝尚右之禮，往復三書，宣布天子威德，辭直氣壯，皆孚筆也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year they reached Annan; the heir Chen Ritong, in mourning observance, did not go out to the suburbs; he sent accompanying ministers to welcome them, and they also did not enter by the Yangming central gate; Zeng and Fu returned to the lodge; they sent a letter rebuking Ritong for the crime of not attending court, and also demanded that Ritong should go out to the suburbs to welcome the edict and discuss the new dynasty's precedence of the right; back and forth three letters; they proclaimed the Son of Heaven's august virtue; the words were straight and the spirit bold—all were Fu's brush.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirtieth year they reached Annan. Heir Chen Ritong, observing mourning, did not go to the suburbs to meet them and sent ministers instead; the envoys were not admitted through the Yangming central gate. Zeng and Fu returned to their lodge and sent letters charging Ritong with failure to attend court, demanding that he meet the imperial edict at the suburbs and discuss the new dynasty's protocol of precedence. Three exchanges of letters proclaimed the Son of Heaven's majesty in language bold and direct—all drafted by Fu.

sentences.zh: 其所贈，孚悉卻之。

translations.literal: What was presented as gifts, Fu entirely refused.
translations.idiomatic: Every gift offered him Fu refused.

sentences.zh: 詳見《梁曾傳》中。

translations.literal: Details are in the biography of Liang Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Liang Zeng.

sentences.zh: 使還，除翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: On return from the mission he was appointed Hanlin Attendant for Drafting, concurrently Compiler at the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the mission he was appointed Hanlin Attendant for Drafting, concurrently Compiler at the National History Office.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲置之要地，而廷臣以孚南人，且尚氣，頗嫉忌之，遂除建德路總管府治中，再遷治中衢州，所至多著善政。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to place him in an important post, but court ministers, because Fu was a southerner and moreover high-spirited, were quite jealous; he was therefore appointed Assistant Administrator of Jiande Circuit; then transferred as Assistant Administrator at Quzhou; wherever he went he largely achieved good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to place him in a key post, but ministers, resenting that he was a southerner and high-spirited, blocked the move. He was made Assistant Administrator of Jiande Circuit, then of Quzhou, and everywhere he served he won a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，復請為鄉郡，特授奉直大夫、台州路總管府治中。

translations.literal: When his term ended he again requested his home district and was specially granted Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and Assistant Administrator of Taizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he asked to return to his home region and was specially granted Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and Assistant Administrator of Taizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，詔遣奉使宣撫循行諸道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade an edict dispatched envoys as Pacification Commissioners to tour the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dade the court dispatched Pacification Commissioners to tour the circuits.

sentences.zh: 時台州旱，民飢，道殣相望，江浙行省檄浙東元帥脫歡察兒發粟賑濟，而脫歡察兒怙勢立威，不恤民隱，驅脅有司，動置重刑，孚曰：「使吾民日至莩死不救者，脫歡察兒也。」

translations.literal: At the time Taizhou suffered drought and the people starved; corpses lined the roads; the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat ordered the Eastern Zhejiang Marshal Tuohuancha'er to distribute grain for relief, but Tuohuancha'er relied on power to stand fierce, cared nothing for the people's plight, drove and coerced officials, and readily imposed heavy punishments; Fu said, "What makes our people die daily like sprats with no rescue is Tuohuancha'er."
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou was then in drought and famine; corpses lined the roads. The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat ordered the Eastern Zhejiang Marshal Tuohuancha'er to distribute relief grain, but he relied on power, ignored the people's suffering, bullied officials, and imposed harsh punishments. Fu said, "The man who lets our people die like fish in a drying pond is Tuohuancha'er."

sentences.zh: 遂詣宣撫使，訴其不法蠹民事一十九條。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to the Pacification Commissioner and reported nineteen items of his unlawful acts harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the Pacification Commissioner and filed nineteen charges of illegal conduct harming the people.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使按實，坐其罪，命有司亟發倉賑饑，民賴以全活者眾，而孚亦以此致疾，卒於家，年六十四。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner verified the facts, convicted him, and ordered the authorities urgently to open the granaries for famine relief; many people relied on this to be preserved alive; Fu also because of this fell ill and died at home, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner verified the charges, convicted Tuohuancha'er, and ordered granaries opened at once. Many lives were saved, but Fu fell ill from the ordeal and died at home at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 孚天材過人，性任俠不羈，其為詩文，大抵任意即成，不事雕斫，有文集行於世。

translations.literal: Fu's natural talent surpassed others; by nature he was chivalrous and unrestrained; in composing poetry and prose he mostly achieved it at will without carving, and had a collected works circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's talent was extraordinary and his nature chivalrous and free. He wrote poetry and prose largely at a stroke without laborious polish, and his collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子遘，江浙行省左右司員外郎，致仕。

translations.literal: His son You served as Vice Director in the Left and Right Sections of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat and retired.
translations.idiomatic: His son You served as Vice Director in the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat and retired.

sentences.zh: 女長媯，適藁城董士楷，太常禮儀院太祝宗緝之母也；

translations.literal: His elder daughter Changgui married Dong Shikai of Gaocheng, mother of Zongji, Grand Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: His elder daughter Changgui married Dong Shikai of Gaocheng and was mother of Zongji, Grand Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 末檀，適同里韓戒之，行樞密院經歷諫之母也。

translations.literal: the younger Tan married Han Jiezhi of the same district, mother of Jian, secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: his younger daughter Tan married Han Jiezhi of the same district and was mother of Jian, secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 俱有貞節，朝廷旌表其門閭。

translations.literal: Both had chaste integrity; the court marked their gate and lane with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Both were celebrated for chaste integrity, and the court marked their gates with commendation.

sentences.zh: 攸州馮子振，其豪俊與孚略同，孚極敬畏之，自以為不可及。

translations.literal: Youzhou's Feng Zizhen was a bold hero much like Fu; Fu greatly revered him and felt himself unable to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zizhen of Youzhou was a bold spirit much like Fu, whom Fu deeply revered and considered beyond his reach.

sentences.zh: 子振於天下之書，無所不記。

translations.literal: Zizhen in books under Heaven had nothing he did not record.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen remembered virtually every book under heaven.

sentences.zh: 當其為文也，酒酣耳熱，命侍史二三人，潤筆以俟，子振據案疾書，隨紙數多寡，頃刻輒盡。

translations.literal: When he composed writing, with wine warm and ears hot he ordered two or three attendants to moisten the brush and wait; Zizhen wrote rapidly at the desk; following however many sheets of paper, in a moment all were finished.
translations.idiomatic: When he wrote, wine warm and spirits high, he had attendants ready the brush and wrote at the desk as fast as paper could be supplied—however many sheets he was given, he finished in moments.

sentences.zh: 雖事料醲鬱，美如簇錦，律之法度，未免乖剌，人亦以此少之。

translations.literal: Though the matter and diction were rich and dense, beautiful as clustered brocade, in law and measure of regulation he could not avoid being contrary, and people for this somewhat slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Though his matter was rich and his diction splendid as brocade, he often fell short of formal standards, and for that people valued him somewhat less.

sentences.zh: 董樸，字太初，順德人。

translations.literal: Dong Pu, style name Taichu, was a native of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Pu, style Taichu, came from Shunde.

sentences.zh: 自幼強記，比冠，師事樂舜諮、劉道濟，幡然有求道之志。

translations.literal: From youth he had a powerful memory; upon reaching manhood he studied under Yue Shunyu and Liu Daoji and suddenly had the will to seek the Way.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he had a powerful memory. At manhood he studied under Yue Shunyu and Liu Daoji and turned with sudden resolve to seeking the Way.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，用提刑按察使薦，起家為陝西知法官。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation of the Surveillance Commissioner, he rose from private life as judicial official of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan the Surveillance Commissioner recommended him, and he entered service as judicial official of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以親老歸養。

translations.literal: Before long, because his parents were old, he returned to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned home to care for his aging parents.

sentences.zh: 尋召為太史院主事，复辭不赴。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as director of the Astronomy Office but again declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as director of the Astronomy Office but again declined.

sentences.zh: 皇慶初，樸年已逾八十，詔以翰林修撰致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangqing, Pu was already past eighty; an edict granted him retirement as Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangqing, when Pu was past eighty, an edict granted him retirement as Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，無疾而終，年八十有五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he died without illness, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanyou he died without prior illness at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 樸所為學，自《六經》及孔、孟微言，與凡先儒所以開端闡幽者，莫不研極其旨而會通之，故其心所自得，往往有融貫之妙。

translations.literal: Pu in learning, from the Six Classics and the subtle words of Confucius and Mencius down to whatever the former Confucians used to open beginnings and clarify obscurities, none were not studied to their purport and brought into unity; therefore what his mind attained for itself often had the subtlety of fusion and penetration.
translations.idiomatic: In learning he pursued the Six Classics and the subtle teachings of Confucius and Mencius, and every method by which earlier Confucians had opened new paths and clarified obscurities, integrating them all. What he attained in his own mind often had the subtlety of full synthesis.

sentences.zh: 其事親孝，與人交，智愚貴賤，一待以誠，或有犯之者，夷然不與之校。

translations.literal: In serving parents he was filial; in dealing with people, whether wise or foolish, noble or base, he treated all with sincerity; if some offended him, he was calmly indifferent and did not contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial to his parents and sincere with everyone he met, wise or foolish, high or low. If someone offended him, he remained calm and would not quarrel.

sentences.zh: 中山王結曰：「樸之學，造詣既深，充養交至；

translations.literal: Prince Jie of Zhongshan said, "Pu's learning has attained both depth of understanding and fullness of cultivation;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jie of Zhongshan said, "Pu's learning has reached both profound understanding and full moral cultivation;

sentences.zh: 其為人，清而通，和而介，君子人也。」

translations.literal: as a man he is clear yet penetrating, harmonious yet firm—a gentleman indeed."
translations.idiomatic: as a man he is clear yet penetrating, harmonious yet principled—a true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 樸家近龍岡，學者因稱​​之曰龍岡先生云。

translations.literal: Pu's home was near Longgang; scholars therefore called him Master Longgang.
translations.idiomatic: Pu lived near Longgang, and scholars called him Master Longgang.

sentences.zh: 楊載，字仲弘，其先居建之浦城，後徙杭，因為杭人。

translations.literal: Yang Zai, style name Zhonghong, his ancestors dwelt in Pucheng of Jian and later migrated to Hang, thus becoming a native of Hang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zai, style Zhonghong, came from Pucheng in Jian; his family later moved to Hangzhou, where he was raised.

sentences.zh: 少孤，博涉群書，為文有跌宕氣。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he broadly mastered many books; in writing he had a quality of bold sweep.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he read widely. His writing had a bold, sweeping quality.

sentences.zh: 年四十，不仕，戶部賈國英數薦於朝，以布衣召為翰林國史院編修官，與修《武宗實錄》，調管領系官海船萬戶府照磨，兼提控案牘。

translations.literal: At age forty he did not serve; Jia Guoying of the Ministry of Revenue repeatedly recommended him to court; as a commoner he was summoned as Compiler at the Hanlin National History Office, participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong, was transferred to registrar of the Office in Charge of Government Sea Ships, and concurrently supervised documents.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he still would not serve. Jia Guoying of the Ministry of Revenue repeatedly recommended him, and he was summoned as a commoner to compile at the Hanlin National History Office, helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong, and was transferred to registrar of the Office in Charge of Government Sea Ships while supervising documents.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，仁宗以科目取士，載首應詔，遂登進士第，授承務郎、饒州路同知浮梁州事，遷儒林郎、寧國路總管府推官以卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou Emperor Renzong took scholars through the examination system; Zai was first to respond to the edict, thereupon passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Gentleman for Attending Affairs and Associate Prefect of Fuliang in Raozhou Circuit, was transferred to Gentleman of the Forest and Assessor of the Ningguo Circuit administration, and died in that post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanyou Emperor Renzong revived the examinations. Zai was the first to answer the call, passed the jinshi, served as Gentleman for Attending Affairs and associate prefect of Fuliang in Raozhou, then as Gentleman of the Forest and assessor in the Ningguo administration, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 初，吳興趙孟頫在翰林，得載所為文，極推重之。

translations.literal: At first Zhao Mengfu of Wuxing, in the Hanlin Academy, obtained writing by Zai and greatly esteemed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Mengfu of Wuxing was in the Hanlin Academy he read Zai's work and esteemed it highly.

sentences.zh: 由是載之文名，隱然動京師，凡所撰述，人多傳誦之。

translations.literal: Thereby Zai's literary name quietly stirred the capital; whatever he composed, many people transmitted and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's literary reputation quietly stirred the capital, and whatever he wrote people copied and recited.

sentences.zh: 其文章一以氣為主，博而敏，直而不肆，自成一家言。

translations.literal: His literary compositions took spirit as their master; broad yet quick, straight yet not unrestrained—they became a school of their own.
translations.idiomatic: His prose took spirit as its master—broad yet nimble, direct yet disciplined—and formed a school of its own.

sentences.zh: 而於詩尤有法，嘗語學者曰：「詩當取材於漢、魏，而音節則以唐為宗。」

translations.literal: In poetry he especially had method; he once told scholars, "Poetry should take material from Han and Wei, while its rhythm and tone should take Tang as its authority."
translations.idiomatic: He was especially methodical in poetry and told students, "Poetry should draw its substance from Han and Wei, but its rhythm and tone should follow the Tang as authority."

sentences.zh: 自其詩出，一冼宋季之陋。

translations.literal: From the time his poetry appeared, it washed clean the vulgarity of the late Song.
translations.idiomatic: Once his poetry appeared it washed away the vulgarity of late-Song verse.

sentences.zh: 建康之上元有楊剛中，字志行，自幼厲志操，及為江東憲府照磨，風采凜凜，有足稱者。

translations.literal: In Shangyuan of Jiankang there was Yang Gangzhong, style Zhixing, who from youth cultivated will and conduct; when he became registrar of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission his bearing was stern and admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gangzhong of Shangyuan in Jiankang, style Zhixing, cultivated moral resolve from youth. As registrar of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission his bearing was stern and admirable.

sentences.zh: 其為文，奇奧簡澀，動法古人，而不屑為世俗平凡語。

translations.literal: In writing he was strange, abstruse, terse, and difficult, always modeling the ancients and disdaining to use the flat language of the vulgar world.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was strange, dense, and difficult, always modeling the ancients and disdaining the flat language of the commonplace world.

sentences.zh: 元明善極嘆異之。

translations.literal: Yuan Mingshan greatly marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mingshan marveled at it deeply.

sentences.zh: 仕至翰林待制而卒。

translations.literal: He served to Hanlin Attendant for Drafting and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin Attendant for Drafting and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 有《霜月集》行於世。

translations.literal: He had the Frost Moon Collection circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Frost Moon Collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 其甥李桓，字晉仲，同郡人，由鄉貢進士，累遷江浙儒學副提舉。

translations.literal: His nephew Li Huan, style Jinzhong, a man of the same prefecture, entered through provincial recommendation as jinshi and was successively promoted to Associate Commissioner for Promoting Confucian Studies in Jiangzhe.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Li Huan, style Jinzhong, from the same prefecture, passed the jinshi by provincial recommendation and rose to Associate Commissioner for Promoting Confucian Studies in Jiangzhe.

sentences.zh: 亦以文鳴江東，紆餘豐潤，學者多傳之。

translations.literal: He too was famed for writing in Jiangdong; his style was ample and lush, and many scholars transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He too was famed for writing in Jiangdong—his style ample and lush, widely copied by scholars.

sentences.zh: 載與剛中同輩行，而桓則稍後云。

translations.literal: Zai and Gangzhong were of the same generation, while Huan came somewhat later.
translations.idiomatic: Zai and Gangzhong were contemporaries; Huan came a generation later.

sentences.zh: 劉詵，字桂翁，吉安之廬陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Shen, style name Guiweng, was a native of Luling in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen, style Guiweng, came from Luling in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 性穎悟，幼失父，知自樹立。

translations.literal: By nature keen and understanding; he lost his father young and knew how to establish himself.
translations.idiomatic: Keen by nature, he lost his father young yet knew how to stand on his own.

sentences.zh: 年十二，作為科場律賦論策之文，蔚然有老成氣象，宋之遺老巨公一見即以斯文之任期之。

translations.literal: At age twelve he composed regulated fu, policy essays, and examination pieces for the examination field; they already had the air of mature mastery; the great old men remaining from the Song, at one sight, all charged him with the mission of this culture.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was already writing examination fu, policy essays, and civil-service pieces with a mature air. Song loyalists at first sight charged him with carrying the literary tradition forward.

sentences.zh: 既冠，重厚醇雅，素以師道自居，教學者有法，聲譽日隆。

translations.literal: After reaching manhood he was weighty, thick, pure, and elegant, always taking the teacher's path as his own; in teaching he had method; his reputation rose daily.
