translations.idiomatic: After reaching manhood he was grave, pure, and refined, always holding himself to the teacher's role. His instruction was methodical and his reputation grew daily.

sentences.zh: 江南行御史臺屢以教官館職、遺逸薦，皆不報。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan Branch Censorate repeatedly recommended him for instructor posts, academy offices, and hidden worthies, but none were answered.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan Branch Censorate repeatedly recommended him for teaching posts, academy offices, and as a hidden worthy, but the court never responded.

sentences.zh: 詵為文，根柢《六經》，躪躒諸子百家，融液今古，而不露其踔厲風發之狀。

translations.literal: Shen in writing took the Six Classics as root, trampled through the hundred schools, fused present and past, yet did not show his leaping, wind-releasing aspect.
translations.idiomatic: His writing rooted in the Six Classics, ranged through the hundred schools, and fused past and present without displaying flashy brilliance.

sentences.zh: 四方求文者，日至於門。

translations.literal: Those from the four quarters who sought his writing came daily to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Seekers of his writing came daily to his gate from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 其所為詩文，曰《桂隱集》。

translations.literal: What he composed in poetry and prose was called the Guixin Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were gathered as the Guixin Collection.

sentences.zh: 桂隱，詵所號也。

translations.literal: Guixin was the style name Shen gave himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guixin was the name he chose for himself.

sentences.zh: 至正十年卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Zhizheng, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Zhizheng at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 同郡龍仁夫，字觀复。

translations.literal: In the same commandery was Long Renfu, styled Guanfu.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow native of the commandery, Long Renfu, styled Guanfu.

sentences.zh: 劉岳申，字高仲。

translations.literal: Liu Yueshen, styled Gaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yueshen, whose style name was Gaozhong.

sentences.zh: 其文學皆與詵齊名，有集行世。

translations.literal: Their literary learning was all equal in fame to Shen's, and they had collections circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Their literary attainments ranked with Liu Shen's, and collections of their work circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 而仁夫之文，尤奇逸流麗，所著《周易集傳》多發前儒之所未發。

translations.literal: Yet Renfu's writing was especially marvelously unrestrained and flowing and elegant, and in his Collected Commentary on the Book of Changes he often brought out what earlier Confucians had not brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Renfu's prose stood out as marvelously free and elegantly flowing, and his Collected Commentary on the Book of Changes broke ground that earlier scholars had left untouched.

sentences.zh: 岳申用薦者為遼陽儒學副提舉，仁夫江浙儒學副提舉，皆不就。

translations.literal: Yueshen, through a recommender, was made Associate Intendant of Confucian Schools in Liaoyang; Renfu was made Associate Intendant of Confucian Schools in the Jiang-Zhe region—neither accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yueshen was recommended for the post of Associate Intendant of Confucian Schools in Liaoyang, and Renfu for the same office in Jiang-Zhe; both declined.

sentences.zh: 韓性，字明善，紹興人。

translations.literal: Han Xing, styled Mingshan, was a man of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xing, styled Mingshan, came from Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 其先家安陽，宋司徒兼侍中魏忠獻王琦，其八世祖也。

translations.literal: His ancestors had their home in Anyang; Wang Qi, Duke of Zhongxian of Wei, Concurrent Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief in the Song, was his eighth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Anyang. His eighth-generation ancestor was Wang Qi, Duke of Zhongxian of Wei, who had served as Song Minister of Works and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 高祖左司郎中膺冑，扈從南渡，家於越。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yingzhou, Left Department Director, followed the court south across the river, and the family settled in Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yingzhou, a Left Department Director, had followed the court in its flight south and settled the family in the Yue region.

sentences.zh: 性天資警敏，七歲讀書，數行俱下，日記萬言。

translations.literal: Xing's inborn gifts were keen and quick; at age seven he read books, several lines at once, and recorded ten thousand words daily from memory.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Xing was exceptionally quick of mind. At seven he could read several lines at a glance and commit ten thousand words to memory in a day.

sentences.zh: 九歲通《小戴禮》，作大義，操筆立就，文意蒼古，老生宿學，皆稱異焉。

translations.literal: At nine he mastered the Elder Dai Record of Rites, wrote expository essays—brush in hand they were instantly complete—and the purport of his writing was austere and ancient; old teachers and veteran scholars all called it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he had mastered the Elder Dai Record of Rites. He could compose expository essays the moment he took up the brush, and the tone of his writing was austere and antique. Veteran teachers marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 及長，博綜群籍，自經史至諸子百氏，靡不極其津涯，究其根柢，而於儒先性理之說，尤深造其閫域。

translations.literal: When grown, he broadly synthesized all books, from the classics and histories to all the schools—there was none to which he did not reach the ford and brink and probe the root and foundation—and in the sayings of earlier Confucians on human nature and principle he especially deeply entered their inner domain.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he mastered an encyclopedic range of literature—from the classics and histories through every school—and pursued each to its foundations. He penetrated deepest of all into the Neo-Confucian doctrine of human nature and principle.

sentences.zh: 其為文辭，博達俊偉，變化不測，自成一家言。

translations.literal: His writings were broad in reach, lofty and grand, changing unpredictably, forming a school of discourse of his own.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was broad, powerful, and ever-shifting in form—a distinctive voice all his own.

sentences.zh: 四方學者，受業其門，戶外之履，至無所容。

translations.literal: Scholars from the four quarters received instruction at his gate; shoes outside the door reached the point where there was no room to contain them.
translations.idiomatic: Students came from every quarter to study with him, and the shoes stacked outside his door soon overflowed the threshold.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，詔以科舉取士，學者多以文法為請，性語之曰：「今之貢舉，悉本硃熹私議，為貢舉之文，不知硃氏之學，可乎？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou, an edict ordered selecting scholars by the civil service examination; many students often requested instruction in examination formulas. Xing told them, "Today's tributes and selections all fundamentally follow Zhu Xi's private interpretations—can one write tribute and selection essays without knowing Zhu Xi's learning?
translations.idiomatic: When Yanyou opened with an edict reviving the examination system, many students asked him to teach exam technique. He told them, "Today's civil examinations all follow Zhu Xi's commentaries. How can you write acceptable examination essays without understanding Zhu Xi's learning?

sentences.zh: 《四書》、《六經》，千載不傳之學，自程氏至硃氏，發明無餘蘊矣，顧行何如耳。

translations.literal: The Four Books and Six Classics are learning not transmitted for a thousand years; from the Cheng brothers to Zhu Xi, the expositions hold no remainder of hidden meaning—one need only look to how one conducts oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Books and Six Classics preserve knowledge that had gone unspoken for a millennium. From the Cheng brothers through Zhu Xi, nothing essential remains unrevealed. What matters is how one lives.

sentences.zh: 有德者必有言，施之場屋，直其末事，豈有他法哉！」

translations.literal: He who has virtue must have words; applying them in the examination hall is simply a lesser matter—is there any other method?"
translations.idiomatic: A man of virtue cannot help but write well. Applying that to the examination hall is a secondary concern. What other method could there be?

sentences.zh: 凡經其口授指畫，不為甚高論而義理自勝，不期文之工而不能不工，以應有司之求，亦未始不合其繩尺也。

translations.literal: Whatever passed his oral instruction and pointing guidance did not make overly lofty arguments yet principle naturally prevailed; he did not expect literary craftsmanship yet could not but be crafted—in meeting the demands of the authorities, neither did it fail to conform to their measuring cords and rules.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever passed through his teaching required no grand theorizing, yet its moral logic always prevailed. He did not strain for literary polish, yet polish came unbidden—and his students' essays met official standards without seeming contrived.

sentences.zh: 士有一善，必為之延譽不已，及辨析是非，則毅然有不可犯之色。

translations.literal: If a gentleman had one good point, he would unceasingly extend praise for him; when discriminating right and wrong, he had a resolute, unassailable bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When a scholar showed even a single virtue, he praised it without end. When he weighed right against wrong, his bearing turned stern and immovable.

sentences.zh: 性出無輿馬僕禦，所過，負者息肩，行者避道。

translations.literal: When Xing went out, there were no carriage, horses, or attending servants; where he passed, those carrying burdens rested their shoulders, and walkers gave way from the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xing never traveled with carriage, horses, or attendants. Wherever he went, porters set down their loads and passersby stepped aside.

sentences.zh: 巷夫街叟，至於童稚廝役，咸稱之曰「韓先生、韓先生」云。

translations.literal: Lane laborers and street old men, down to children and menial servants, all called him "Master Han, Master Han."
translations.idiomatic: Laborers in the lanes, elders in the streets, even children and servants—all called him "Master Han, Master Han."

sentences.zh: 憲府嘗舉為教官，謝曰：「幸有先人之敝廬可庇風雨，薄田可具饘粥，讀書砥行，無愧古人足矣，祿仕非所願也。」

translations.literal: The surveillance commission once recommended him as instructor; he declined, saying, "Fortunately I have my ancestors' humble dwelling to shelter from wind and rain, and meager fields to supply porridge. Reading books and honing conduct so as not to shame the ancients is enough; salary and office are not my wish."
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commission once recommended him as a school instructor. He declined: "My ancestors left a humble roof against wind and rain and enough land for simple meals. To read and cultivate character without shaming the ancients is enough. I have no wish for salary or office.

sentences.zh: 受而不赴。

translations.literal: He accepted the appointment but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the appointment in name but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 暮年愈自韜晦，然未嘗忘情於斯世，郡之良二千石政事有所未達，輒往諮訪，性從容載導，洞中肯綮，裨益者多。

translations.literal: In his later years he withdrew further into concealment, yet never lost feeling for this world; when the commandery's able two-thousand-shi officials had affairs they had not grasped, they would go to consult him, and Xing with easy bearing would carry forth guidance, penetrating to the vital joint—many benefited.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he grew still more retiring, yet he never ceased caring for the world. When able county prefects found themselves at a loss in governance, they sought his counsel. Xing guided them with unhurried ease, always striking the vital point—and many were the better for it.

sentences.zh: 天歷中，趙世延以性名上聞。

translations.literal: During Tianli, Zhao Shiyan reported Xing's name to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianli era, Zhao Shiyan brought Xing's name to the court's attention.

sentences.zh: 後十年，門人李齊為南台監察御史，力舉其行義，而性已卒矣。

translations.literal: Ten years later, his disciple Li Qi was Surveillance Censor of the Southern Commission and vigorously commended his conduct and righteousness, but Xing had already died.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later his disciple Li Qi, serving as Surveillance Censor of the Southern Commission, vigorously commended his moral character—but Xing was already dead.

sentences.zh: 年七十有六。

translations.literal: His age was seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-six years old.

sentences.zh: 卒後，南台御史右丞月魯不花，嘗學於性，言性法當得諡，朝廷賜諡莊節先生。

translations.literal: After death, Yue Lu Bulhua, Right Vice Censor of the Southern Commission, who had once studied with Xing, said Xing by law ought to receive a posthumous title; the court bestowed the posthumous title Master Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Yue Lu Bulhua of the Southern Censorate, who had once been his student, argued that Xing deserved a posthumous honor. The court granted him the title Master Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 其所著有《禮記說》四卷，《詩音釋》一卷，《書辨疑》一卷，《郡志》八卷，文集十二卷。

translations.literal: What he authored included four juan of Record of Rites Explanations, one juan of Poetry Phonology Explanations, one juan of Documents Doubts Resolved, eight juan of Commandery Gazetteer, and twelve juan of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Record of Rites Explanations in four juan, Poetry Phonology Explanations in one juan, Documents Doubts Resolved in one juan, a Commandery Gazetteer in eight juan, and twelve juan of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 當性時，慶元有程端禮、端學兄弟者。

translations.literal: In Xing's time, in Qingyuan there were the brothers Cheng Duanli and Cheng Duanxue.
translations.idiomatic: During Xing's lifetime, Qingyuan produced the brothers Cheng Duanli and Cheng Duanxue.

sentences.zh: 端禮，字敬叔，幼穎悟純篤，十五歲，能記誦《六經》，曉析大義。

translations.literal: Duanli, styled Jingshu, in youth was keenly perceptive, pure and sincere; at fifteen he could memorize and recite the Six Classics and clearly analyze their great meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli, styled Jingshu, was bright and sincere from boyhood. By fifteen he had memorized the Six Classics and could expound their major themes with clarity.

sentences.zh: 慶元自宋季皆尊尚陸九淵氏之學，而硃熹氏學不行於慶元。

translations.literal: Qingyuan from the late Song all honored and upheld Lu Jiuyuan's learning, while Zhu Xi's learning did not prevail in Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Song, Qingyuan had honored the learning of Lu Jiuyuan, and Zhu Xi's teachings had never taken root there.

sentences.zh: 端禮獨從史蒙卿遊，以傳硃氏明體達用之指，學者及門甚眾。

translations.literal: Duanli alone followed Shi Mengqing in study, to transmit Zhu Xi's aim of clarifying substance and reaching to practice; scholars who reached his gate were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli alone studied under Shi Mengqing and passed on Zhu Xi's teaching on discerning substance and putting it into practice. A great throng of students came to his door.

sentences.zh: 所著有《讀書工程》，國子監以頒示郡邑校官，為學者式。

translations.literal: What he authored included Methods of Reading Books; the Directorate of Education distributed it to county and district school officers as a model for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Methods of Reading Books, which the Directorate of Education circulated among local school officials as a model for students.

sentences.zh: 仕為衢州路儒學教授。

translations.literal: He served as Professor of Confucian Learning in Quzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Professor of Confucian Learning at Quzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十五。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 端學，字時叔，通《春秋》，登至治辛酉進士第，授仙居縣丞，尋改國子助教。

translations.literal: Duanxue, styled Shishu, mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, passed the jinshi examination in the xinyou year of Zhizhi, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xianju County, and soon transferred to be Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Duanxue, styled Shishu, mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, passed the jinshi examination in the xinyou year of Zhizhi, was appointed deputy magistrate of Xianju County, and was soon transferred to Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 動有師法，學者以其剛嚴方正，咸嚴憚之。

translations.literal: In every movement he had teachers' methods; scholars, because he was stern, strict, and upright, all stood in awe before him.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted himself by strict pedagogical standards, and students held him in awe for his stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，命未下而卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but before the order was issued he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but died before the appointment could take effect.

sentences.zh: 後以子徐貴，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Later, because his son Xu was honored, he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his son Xu achieved distinction, he was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 所著有《春秋本義》三十卷，《三傳辨疑》二十卷，《春秋或問》十卷。

translations.literal: What he authored included thirty juan of Original Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, twenty juan of Doubts on the Three Commentaries Resolved, and ten juan of Questions on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Original Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals in thirty juan, Doubts on the Three Commentaries Resolved in twenty juan, and Questions on the Spring and Autumn Annals in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 吳師道，字正傳，婺州蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Wu Shidao, styled Zhengchuan, was a man of Lanxi in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shidao, styled Zhengchuan, came from Lanxi in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 自羈狖知學，即善記覽。

translations.literal: From infancy when he knew learning, he was adept at memorizing what he read.
translations.idiomatic: From the age when he first understood learning, he possessed a prodigious memory.

sentences.zh: 工詞章，才思湧溢，發為歌詩，清麗俊逸。

translations.literal: He was skilled in literary composition; talent and thought surged forth—when released as songs and poems, they were clear, beautiful, lofty, and unbound.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at literary composition, his talent flowing freely. His poetry was clear, elegant, and spirited.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，因讀宋儒真德秀遺書，乃幡然有志於為己之學，刮摩淬礪，日長月益，嘗以持敬致知之說質於同郡許謙，謙復之以理一分殊之旨，由是心志益廣，造履益深，大抵務在發揮義理，而以辟異端為先務。

translations.literal: At weak-cap age, through reading the posthumous writings of the Song Confucian Zhen Dexiu, he then suddenly had resolve toward learning for oneself, scraping and sharpening, growing day by day and month by month; he once submitted to Xu Qian of the same commandery his views on maintaining reverence and extending knowledge, and Qian replied with the purport of principle as one yet differentiated in manifestation; thereby his mind and will grew broader and his attainment and conduct grew deeper—in general he strove to develop principle and righteousness, and took repelling heterodox teachings as the first task.
translations.idiomatic: In young manhood, reading the posthumous works of the Song Neo-Confucian Zhen Dexiu stirred in him a resolve to pursue learning for its own sake. He honed himself day after day, month after month. He once submitted to fellow Lanxi scholar Xu Qian his understanding of maintaining reverence and extending knowledge; Qian answered with the doctrine of principle as one yet manifest in many particulars. His intellectual horizons broadened and his moral practice deepened. He devoted himself above all to explicating moral principle, making the refutation of heterodox teachings his first concern.

sentences.zh: 登至治元年進士第，授高郵縣丞，明達文法，吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhizhi, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Gaoyou County; he was clear and penetrating in statutory law, and clerks did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhizhi and was appointed deputy magistrate of Gaoyou County. Thoroughly versed in administrative law, he ran an office his clerks dared not cheat.

sentences.zh: 再調寧國路錄事。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be Record Keeper of Ningguo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was next assigned as Record Keeper of Ningguo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會歲大旱，饑民仰食於官者三十三萬口，師道勸大家得粟三萬七千六百石，以賑饑民；

translations.literal: It happened that year there was great drought; famine victims relying on official grain numbered three hundred thirty thousand mouths. Shidao persuaded the great households to obtain thirty-seven thousand six hundred shi of grain to relieve the famine victims;
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe drought. Three hundred thirty thousand people depended on official relief. Shidao persuaded wealthy families to contribute thirty-seven thousand six hundred shi of grain for famine relief;

sentences.zh: 又言於部使者，轉聞於朝，得粟四萬石、鈔三萬八千四百錠賑之，三十餘萬人賴以存活。

translations.literal: He also spoke to the circuit envoy, who relayed it to the court, and obtained forty thousand shi of grain and thirty-eight thousand four hundred ingots of paper money for relief; more than three hundred thousand people relied on this to survive.
translations.idiomatic: He also appealed to the circuit commissioner, who forwarded the matter to court. The court allocated forty thousand shi of grain and thirty-eight thousand four hundred ingots of paper currency for relief—and more than three hundred thousand lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 遷池州建德縣尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Magistrate of Jiande County in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jiande County in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 郡學有田七百畝，為豪民所佔，郡下其事建德，俾師道究治之，即為按其圖籍，悉以歸於學。

translations.literal: The prefectural school had seven hundred mu of fields occupied by powerful locals; the prefecture sent the matter down to Jiande and had Shidao investigate and settle it; he immediately examined the register maps and restored all to the school.
translations.idiomatic: Local magnates had seized seven hundred mu belonging to the prefectural school. The prefecture referred the case to Jiande for investigation, and Shidao checked the land registers and restored every plot to the school.

sentences.zh: 建德素少茶，而榷稅尤重，民以為病，即為極言於所司，榷稅為減。

translations.literal: Jiande had always had little tea, yet monopoly tax was especially heavy—the people took it as affliction; he immediately spoke forcefully to the responsible office, and the monopoly tax was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande produced little tea yet bore an especially heavy monopoly tax—a burden on the people. Shidao pressed the authorities vigorously, and the tax was reduced.

sentences.zh: 中書左丞呂思誠、侍御史孔思立列薦之，召為國子助教，尋升博士。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor of the Secretariat Lu Sicheng and Attending Censor Kong Sili jointly recommended him; he was summoned as Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education, and soon promoted to Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Lu Sicheng and Attending Censor Kong Sili jointly recommended him. He was summoned to the Directorate of Education as Assistant Instructor and soon promoted to Doctor.

sentences.zh: 其為教，一本硃熹之旨，而遵許衡之成法，六館諸生，人人自以為得師。

translations.literal: His teaching took Zhu Xi's aim as the single root and followed Xu Heng's established methods; students of the six halls each considered themselves to have found a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He taught according to Zhu Xi's principles and Xu Heng's established methods. Every student in the six halls felt he had at last found a true master.

sentences.zh: 丁內憂而歸，以奉議大夫、禮部郎中致仕，終於家。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother he returned home, retired with the ranks of Supporter of the Discussion Grand Master and Director in the Ministry of Rites, and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home upon his mother's death, retired with the ranks of Supporter of Discussion Grand Master and Director in the Ministry of Rites, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 所著有《易詩書雜說》、《春秋胡傳附辨》、《戰國策校注》、《敬鄉錄》，及文集二十卷。

translations.literal: What he authored included Miscellaneous Explanations of the Changes, Poetry, and Documents, Supplementary Critique of Hu Yuan's Spring and Autumn Commentary, Collation and Annotation of the Intrigues of the Warring States, Records of Respected Natives of the District, and twenty juan of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: His publications included Miscellaneous Explanations of the Changes, Poetry, and Documents; Supplementary Critique of Hu Yuan's Spring and Autumn Commentary; Collation and Annotation of the Intrigues of the Warring States; Records of Respected Natives of the District; and twenty juan of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 師道同郡又有王餘慶，字叔善，仕為江南行台監察御史，亦以儒學名重當世云。

translations.literal: In Shidao's commandery there was also Wang Yuqing, styled Shushan, who served as Surveillance Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat—also renowned in his generation for Confucian learning, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow native, Wang Yuqing, styled Shushan, served as Surveillance Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and was likewise celebrated in his day for Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 陸文圭，字子方，江陰人。

translations.literal: Lu Wengui, styled Zifang, was a man of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wengui, styled Zifang, came from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 幼而穎悟，讀書過目成誦，終身不忘。

translations.literal: In youth he was keenly perceptive; what he read passed before his eyes and became recitation; he never forgot it through life.
translations.idiomatic: Bright from childhood, he could read a passage once and recite it from memory—and never forgot what he had learned.

sentences.zh: 博通經史百家，及天文、地理、律曆、醫藥、算數之學。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered the classics, histories, and hundred schools, as well as astronomy, geography, calendrical science, medicine, and mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and histories, the hundred schools, and disciplines from astronomy, geography, and calendrics to medicine and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 宋咸淳初，文圭年十八，以《春秋》中鄉選。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianchun in the Song, Wengui was eighteen and passed the prefectural selection with the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianchun era of the Song, at eighteen he passed the provincial selection with the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，隱居城東，學者稱之曰牆東先生。

translations.literal: When the Song perished, he lived in seclusion east of the city; scholars called him Master East of the Wall.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Song he retired to seclusion east of the city, and scholars called him Master East of the Wall.

sentences.zh: 延祐設科，有司強之就試，凡一再中鄉舉。

translations.literal: When Yanyou established the examinations, the authorities forced him to try; in all he twice passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yanyou examinations were instituted, officials pressed him to compete—and he twice passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 文圭為文，融會經傳，縱橫變化，莫測其涯際，東南學者，皆宗師之。

translations.literal: Wengui in writing fused the classics and commentaries, ranging and changing—their shore could not be measured; scholars of the southeast all took him as ancestral teacher.
translations.idiomatic: His writing synthesized the classics with boundless versatility. Scholars throughout the southeast looked to him as their master.

sentences.zh: 朝廷數遣使馳幣聘之，以老疾，不果行。

translations.literal: The court several times sent envoys with swift gifts to engage him; because of old age and illness, he did not in the end go.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly sent envoys with gifts to summon him, but age and illness kept him from accepting.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十五。

translations.literal: He died aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 文圭為人，剛明超邁，以奇氣自負。

translations.literal: Wengui as a person was firm, clear, transcendent, and bold—he took pride in his exceptional spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui was forthright, luminous, and bold—a man who carried himself with uncommon force of character.

sentences.zh: 於地理考核甚詳，凡天下郡縣沿革、人物土產，悉能默記，如指諸掌。

translations.literal: In geographical investigation he was very detailed; all the changes of commanderies and counties under heaven, personages, and local products—he could silently memorize all, as if pointing to them on his palm.
translations.idiomatic: His knowledge of geography was exhaustive: he could recite from memory every change in the administrative map, every notable figure and local product—as if they lay in the palm of his hand.

sentences.zh: 先屬纊一日，語門人曰：「以數考之，吾州二十年後必有兵變，慘於五代、建炎，吾死，當葬不食之地，勿封勿樹，使人不知吾墓，庶無暴骨之患。」

translations.literal: One day before laying on the hempen mourning cloth, he told his disciples, "Examining by numbers, our prefecture twenty years hence will surely have military turmoil, more bitter than the Five Dynasties and the Jianyan era. When I die, bury me in barren land; do not mound, do not plant trees—let people not know my tomb, that perhaps there will be no calamity of exposed bones."
translations.idiomatic: A day before his final illness, he told his disciples: "By my calculations, this prefecture will suffer military calamity within twenty years—worse than the Five Dynasties or the Jianyan reign. When I die, bury me in desolate ground. Raise no mound, plant no tree. Let no one know where I lie, so that my bones may escape desecration.

sentences.zh: 其後江陰之亂，塚墓盡發，人乃服其先知。

translations.literal: Later, in the Jiangyin turmoil, tombs and graves were all opened; people then submitted to his foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion later swept Jiangyin and graves were despoiled across the region, people came to respect his prescience.

sentences.zh: 有《牆東類稿》二十卷。

translations.literal: He had the Miscellaneous Drafts East of the Wall in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left Miscellaneous Drafts East of the Wall in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 文圭同里有梁益者，字友直，其先福州人。

translations.literal: In Wengui's neighborhood there was Liang Yi, styled Youzhi; his ancestors were men of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor of Wengui's, Liang Yi, styled Youzhi, came from a Fuzhou family.

sentences.zh: 博洽經史，而工於文辭。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories, and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply versed in the classics and histories and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 其教人，以變化氣質為先務，學徒不遠千里從之。

translations.literal: In teaching people, transforming one's inherent disposition was the first task; disciples came from beyond a thousand li to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He taught that transforming one's character came first, and students traveled from afar to study with him.

sentences.zh: 自文圭既卒，浙以西稱學術醇正、為世師表者，惟益而已。

translations.literal: Since Wengui had already died, west of Zhe those called pure and correct in learning and the age's model teachers were only Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Wengui's death, Liang Yi alone west of Zhe was regarded as the standard-bearer of pure scholarship and moral example.

sentences.zh: 益所著書，有《三山稿》、《詩緒餘》、《史傳姓氏纂》，又有《詩傳旁通》，發揮硃熹氏之學為精。

translations.literal: Books Yi authored included Three Mountains Drafts, Remaining Threads of Poetry, Compilation of Surnames in Historical Biographies, and also Poetic Commentary Side Paths—expounding Zhu Xi's learning with refinement.
translations.idiomatic: His books included Three Mountains Drafts, Remaining Threads of Poetry, and Compilation of Surnames in Historical Biographies, as well as Poetic Commentary Side Paths, a refined exposition of Zhu Xi's learning.

sentences.zh: 年五十六卒。

translations.literal: He died aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 周仁榮，字本心，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Zhou Renrong, styled Benxin, was a man of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Renrong, styled Benxin, came from Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 父敬孫，宋太學生。

translations.literal: His father Jingsun was a student of the Song Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingsun had been a student at the Song Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 初，金華王柏以硃熹之學主台之上蔡書院，敬孫與同郡楊珏、陳天瑞、車若水、黃超然、硃致中、薛松年師事之，受性理之旨。

translations.literal: Initially, Wang Bo of Jinhua, with Zhu Xi's learning, headed Shangcai Academy on Mount Tai; Jingsun, together with Yang Jue, Chen Tianrui, Che Ruoshui, Huang Chaoran, Zhu Zhizhong, and Xue Songnian of the same commandery, took him as teacher in attendance and received the purport of human nature and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Wang Bo of Jinhua, a champion of Zhu Xi's learning, directed Shangcai Academy on Mount Tai. Jingsun, along with fellow natives Yang Jue, Chen Tianrui, Che Ruoshui, Huang Chaoran, Zhu Zhizhong, and Xue Songnian, studied under him and received instruction in Neo-Confucian doctrine.

sentences.zh: 敬孫嘗著《易象佔》、《尚書補遺》、《春秋類例》。

translations.literal: Jingsun once authored Images and Divination in the Changes, Supplementary Remnants of the Documents, and Categories and Examples of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsun wrote Images and Divination in the Changes, Supplementary Remnants of the Documents, and Categories and Examples of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 仁榮承其家學，又師珏、天瑞，治《易》、《禮》、《春秋》，而工為文章。

translations.literal: Renrong inherited his family's learning, and also took Jue and Tianrui as teachers, studying the Changes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Renrong inherited the family tradition and also studied under Yang Jue and Chen Tianrui, mastering the Changes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals while excelling as a writer.

sentences.zh: 用薦者署美化書院山長。

translations.literal: Through a recommender he was appointed as director of Meihua Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was appointed director of Meihua Academy.

sentences.zh: 美化在處州萬山中，人鮮知學，仁榮舉行鄉飲酒禮，士俗為變。

translations.literal: Meihua was in the myriad mountains of Chuzhou; people rarely knew learning; Renrong conducted the district drinking ceremony, and gentry customs were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Meihua lay deep in the mountains of Chuzhou, where learning was scarcely known. Renrong introduced the district drinking ceremony, and local mores began to change.

sentences.zh: 後辟江浙行省掾史，省臣皆呼先生，不以吏遇之。

translations.literal: Later he was recruited as clerk of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; secretariat ministers all called him Master and did not treat him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed clerk of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, where senior officials addressed him as Master and never treated him as a mere functionary.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，召拜國子博士，遷翰林修撰，升集賢待制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding, he was summoned and appointed Doctor at the Directorate of Education, transferred to Hanlin Compiler, and promoted to Attendant Drafting Scholar at the Academy of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiding era he was summoned as Doctor at the Directorate of Education, transferred to Hanlin Compiler, and raised to Attendant Drafting Scholar at the Academy of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 奉旨代祀岳瀆，至會稽，以疾作，不復還朝。

translations.literal: By imperial order he performed sacrifice in lieu at the mountains and rivers; reaching Kuaiji, illness arose, and he did not return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to perform ritual sacrifices to the sacred mountains and rivers, he fell ill at Kuaiji and never returned to court.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十有一。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 其所教弟子多為名人，而泰不華實為進士第一。

translations.literal: Among the disciples he taught, many became notable men, and Tai Bughua in fact placed first in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his students rose to prominence—the jinshi examination's top graduate, Tai Bughua, was among them.

sentences.zh: 其弟仔肩，字本道，以《春秋》登延祐五年進士第，終奉議大夫、惠州路總管府判官。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zijian, styled Bendao, passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Yanyou with the Spring and Autumn Annals, and ended as Supporter of the Discussion Grand Master and Administrative Assistant of the Huizhou Circuit General Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zijian, styled Bendao, passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Yanyou with the Spring and Autumn Annals and retired as Supporter of Discussion Grand Master and Administrative Assistant of Huizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 與其兄俱以文學名。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother were both famed for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother were both celebrated for literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 仁榮同郡有孟夢恂者，字長文，黃岩人。

translations.literal: In Renrong's commandery there was Meng Mengxun, styled Changwen, a man of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow native of Renrong's, Meng Mengxun, styled Changwen, came from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 與仁榮同師事楊珏、陳天瑞。

translations.literal: He and Renrong alike took Yang Jue and Chen Tianrui as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Yang Jue and Chen Tianrui alongside Renrong.

sentences.zh: 夢恂講解經旨，體認精切，務見行事，四方游從者皆服焉。

translations.literal: Mengxun in expounding the classics' purport had precise, incisive embodied comprehension, striving to see it in conduct; wanderers who followed from the four quarters all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun expounded the classics with exacting clarity and insisted that understanding show itself in action. Students who came from every direction respected him deeply.

sentences.zh: 部使者薦其行義，署本郡學錄。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy recommended his conduct and righteousness, and he was appointed Registrar of the commandery school.
translations.idiomatic: A circuit commissioner recommended him for his moral character, and he was appointed Registrar of the local Confucian school.

sentences.zh: 至正十三年，以設策禦寇救鄉郡有功，授登仕郎、常州路宜興州判官，未受命而卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhizheng, for devising stratagems to repel bandits and saving the home commandery with merit, he was granted Dengshi Gentleman and Administrative Assistant of Yixing Prefecture in Changzhou Circuit; before receiving the appointment he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhizheng he was rewarded for organizing defenses against bandits and saving his home commandery with the rank of Dengshi Gentleman and appointment as Administrative Assistant of Yixing in Changzhou Circuit. He died before taking office, at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賜諡號曰康靖先生。

translations.literal: The court granted the posthumous title Master Kangjing.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him as Master Kangjing.

sentences.zh: 所著有《性理本旨》、《四書辨疑》、《漢唐會要》、《七政疑解》，及《筆海雜錄》五十卷。

translations.literal: What he authored included Original Purport of Human Nature and Principle, Doubts on the Four Books Resolved, Essentials of Han and Tang Institutions, Doubts on the Seven Regulators Resolved, and Miscellaneous Records of the Brush Sea in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Original Purport of Human Nature and Principle, Doubts on the Four Books Resolved, Essentials of Han and Tang Institutions, Doubts on the Seven Regulators Resolved, and Miscellaneous Records of the Brush Sea in fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 陳旅，字眾仲，興化莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Lü, styled Zhongzhong, was a man of Putian in Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lü, styled Zhongzhong, came from Putian in Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 先世素以儒學稱。

translations.literal: For generations his forebears were known for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been respected for Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 旅幼孤，資禀穎異。

translations.literal: Lü lost his father in youth; his native endowment was keen and extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lü was orphaned young, yet his natural gifts were remarkably sharp.

sentences.zh: 其外大父趙氏學有源委，撫而教之，旅得所依，不以生業為務，惟篤志於學，於書無所不讀。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather of the Zhao clan had learning with deep roots; he nurtured and taught him, and Lü found a place to rely upon. He did not take livelihood as his occupation, but devoted his will solely to learning, and in books there was nothing he did not read.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather, a Zhao, was a scholar of deep learning who raised and instructed him, giving Chen Lü a secure home. He cared nothing for making a living and devoted himself entirely to study, reading every book he could find.

sentences.zh: 稍長，負笈至溫陵，從鄉先生傅古直遊，聲名日著。

translations.literal: When he had grown somewhat, he shouldered his book-chest and went to Wenling, following the local elder Fu Guzhi in study; his reputation daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured, he traveled with his books to Wenling to study under the local master Fu Guzhi, and his fame spread steadily.

sentences.zh: 用薦者為閩海儒學官，適御史中丞馬雍古祖常使泉南，一見奇之，謂旅曰：「子，館閣器也，胡為留滯於此！」

translations.literal: Through recommendation he became Confucian school official of Minhai. It happened that Censor-in-Chief Ma Yonggu Zuchang was envoy to the south of Quanzhou; at first sight he considered him extraordinary, and said to Lü: "You, sir, are material for the Academy halls—why linger stagnating here!"
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for office, he was appointed Confucian instructor in Minhai. The censor-in-chief Ma Zuchang happened to be on mission in southern Quanzhou; at their first meeting he was struck by Chen Lü and said, "You are fit for the Hanlin Academy—why remain stuck in this backwater?"

sentences.zh: 因相勉遊京師。

translations.literal: He thereupon urged each other to travel to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Chen Lü to go to the capital, and they encouraged each other to make the journey.

sentences.zh: 既至，翰林侍講學士虞集見其所為文，既然歎曰：「此所謂我老將休，付子斯文者矣。」

translations.literal: When he had arrived, Hanlin Academy Lecturing Scholar Yu Ji saw the writings he had composed and, sighing deeply, said: "This is what is meant by 'I am old and about to rest—this culture I entrust to you.'
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the capital, the Hanlin lecturer Yu Ji read his essays and sighed with deep emotion: "This is what people mean when they say, 'I am old and ready to step aside—I leave this literary tradition in your hands.'

sentences.zh: 即延至館中，朝夕以道義學問相講習，自謂得旅之助為多。

translations.literal: He at once invited him to his residence, morning and evening discussing and practicing together in moral principle and learning, and declared that he had gained much assistance from Lü.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately invited Chen Lü to stay at his home, and they spent their days debating ethics and scholarship. Yu Ji later said he had benefited enormously from their exchanges.

sentences.zh: 與祖常交口遊譽於諸公間，咸以為旅博學多聞，宜居師範之選，中書平章政事趙世延又力荐之，除國子助教。

translations.literal: Together with Zuchang they spoke in turn, traveling in praise among the great officials; all considered that Lü was broadly learned and well informed and ought to occupy a choice post as teacher-model. Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat Zhao Shiyan again strongly recommended him, and he was appointed Associate Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zuchang spoke warmly of each other among the capital's leading men, and all agreed that Chen Lü's erudition made him ideal for a teaching post. Grand Councillor Zhao Shiyan added his strong recommendation, and Chen Lü was appointed Associate Instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 居三年，考滿，諸生不忍其去，請於朝，再任焉。

translations.literal: He served three years; when his term evaluation was complete, the students could not bear his departure and petitioned the court, and he was reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, when his term ended, his students begged the court to keep him—and he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，出為江浙儒學副提舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong, he went out as Assistant Commissioner for Confucian Schools in Jiangzhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuantong he was posted as Assistant Commissioner for Confucian Schools in Jiangzhe.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，入為應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan, he entered as Hanlin Academy Document Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he returned to the capital as a Hanlin document-drafting official.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，遷國子監丞，階文林郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng, he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy, with rank as Gentleman of Literary Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizheng he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy with the rank of Gentleman of Literary Eminence.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒，年五十有六。

translations.literal: Two years later he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died, at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 旅於文，自先秦以來，至唐、宋諸大家，無所不究，故其文典雅峻潔，必求合於古作者，不徒以徇世好而已。

translations.literal: In literature, Lü from the pre-Qin onward down to the great masters of Tang and Song investigated without exception; therefore his writing was elegant, lofty, and pure, always seeking accord with ancient authors, not merely currying worldly favor.
translations.idiomatic: In his writing Chen Lü studied every major author from pre-Qin times through the Tang and Song masters. His prose was elegant, rigorous, and polished; he aimed to match the ancients rather than chase contemporary taste.

sentences.zh: 有文集十四卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in fourteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to fourteen juan.

sentences.zh: 旅平生於師友之義尤篤，每感虞集為知己。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Lü was especially devoted to the obligations between teacher and friend, and always felt gratitude that Yu Ji was his intimate knower.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lü was deeply devoted to the bonds of teacher and friend, and always regarded Yu Ji as the truest friend of his life.

sentences.zh: 其在浙江時，集歸田已數載，歲且大比，請於行省參知政事孛術魯翀，親奉書幣，請集主文鄉闈，欲為​​問候計，乃衝冒炎暑，千里訪集於臨川。

translations.literal: When he was in Zhejiang, Ji had returned to fields already several years. The year being the great provincial examination, he requested of the Branch Secretariat's Vice Administrator Bo Shilu Chong, personally bearing letter and gifts, to ask Ji to preside over the essays in the provincial examination hall—intending it as a plan to pay respects—and braving the blazing heat traveled a thousand li to visit Ji at Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Zhejiang, Chen Lü learned that Yu Ji had been living in retirement for several years. When the provincial examinations drew near, he asked the vice administrator Bo Shilu Chong for permission to deliver a formal invitation—and then, braving the midsummer heat, traveled a thousand li to Linchuan simply to see his old mentor again.

sentences.zh: 集感其來，留旬日而別，惓藐以斯文相勉，慘然若將永訣焉。

translations.literal: Ji was moved by his coming, kept him ten days and then parted, earnestly and tenderly urging each other in this culture, mournful as if about to bid eternal farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji was deeply moved by the visit and kept him for ten days. They parted with earnest encouragement to carry on the literary tradition, both sorrowful as though they would never meet again.

sentences.zh: 集每與學者語，必以旅為平生益友也。

translations.literal: Whenever Ji spoke with scholars, he always spoke of Lü as the beneficial friend of his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yu Ji spoke with fellow scholars, he called Chen Lü the finest friend of his life.

sentences.zh: 一日，夢旅舉杯相向曰：「旅甚思公，亦知公之不忘旅也，但不得見爾。」

translations.literal: One day he dreamed that Lü raised a cup facing him and said: "Lü greatly misses you, and also knows that you do not forget Lü—only we cannot meet, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed that Chen Lü raised a cup toward him and said, "I miss you deeply, and I know you have not forgotten me—we simply cannot see each other anymore."

sentences.zh: 既而聞旅卒，集深悼之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he heard that Lü had died, and Ji deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he learned that Chen Lü had died, and Yu Ji grieved profoundly.

sentences.zh: 同時有程文、陳繹曾者，皆名士。

translations.literal: At the same time there were Cheng Wen and Chen Yiceng, both famed scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries of comparable stature included Cheng Wen and Chen Yiceng, both celebrated scholars.

sentences.zh: 文字以文，徽州人，仕至禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Cheng Wen, styled Yiwen, was a man of Huizhou; in office he reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wen, styled Yiwen, came from Huizhou and rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 作文明潔而精深，集亦多稱之。

translations.literal: His compositions were lucid and refined yet profound; Ji also often praised them.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was clear, polished, and deeply learned, and Yu Ji spoke highly of it.

sentences.zh: 繹曾字伯敷，處州人。

translations.literal: Yiceng, styled Bofu, was a man of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yiceng, styled Bofu, came from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為人雖口吃，而精敏異常，諸經註疏，多能成誦。

translations.literal: As a man, though he stuttered, he was extraordinarily keen and quick; commentaries on the various classics he could for the most part recite complete.
translations.idiomatic: Though he stuttered when he spoke, his mind was exceptionally sharp—he could recite most classical commentaries from memory.

sentences.zh: 文辭汪洋浩博，其氣燁如也。

translations.literal: His literary language was vast, overflowing, and boundless; its spirit blazed brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was expansive and richly learned, written with blazing vitality.

sentences.zh: 官至國子助教。

translations.literal: In office he reached Associate Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of Associate Instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 論者謂二人皆與旅相伯仲云。

translations.literal: Critics said that both men were matched with Lü as equals.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries considered both men Chen Lü's equals in talent.

sentences.zh: 李孝光，字季和，溫州樂清人。

translations.literal: Li Xiaoguang, styled Jihe, was a man of Yueqing in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoguang, styled Jihe, came from Yueqing in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少博學，篤志復古，隱居雁蕩山五峰下，四方之士，遠來受學，名譽日聞，泰不華以師事之，南行台監察御史闔辭屢薦居館閣。

translations.literal: From youth he was broadly learned and devoted his will to restoring antiquity. He lived in seclusion beneath the Five Peaks of Yandang Mountain; scholars from the four quarters came from afar to receive instruction, and his fame daily spread. Tai Bughua took him as teacher, and the Southern Branch Censor He Ci repeatedly recommended him for residence in the Academy halls.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was widely read and devoted to reviving ancient literary standards. He lived in seclusion beneath the Five Peaks of Yandang Mountain, where students traveled from every direction to study with him. Tai Bughua became his disciple, and the southern censor He Ci repeatedly recommended him for appointment to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 至正七年，詔徵隱士，以秘書監著作郎召，與完者圖、執禮哈瑯、董立同應詔赴京師，見帝於宣文閣，進《孝經圖說》，帝大悅，賜上尊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng, an edict summoned recluses; he was summoned as Drafting Official of the Secretariat Directorate, and together with Wanzhitu, Zhili Halang, and Dong Li responded to the edict and went to the capital. He saw the emperor at the Hall of Propagating Culture, presented the Illustrated Exposition of the Classic of Filial Piety, and the emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed superior wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhizheng the court issued a call for reclusive scholars, and Li Xiaoguang was summoned as Drafting Official of the Secretariat Directorate. He traveled to the capital with Wanzhitu, Zhili Halang, and Dong Li, was received by the emperor in the Hall of Propagating Culture, and presented his Illustrated Exposition of the Classic of Filial Piety. The emperor was delighted and rewarded him with fine wine.

sentences.zh: 明年，昇文林郎、秘書監丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Gentleman of Literary Eminence and Assistant Director of the Secretariat Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Gentleman of Literary Eminence and Assistant Director of the Secretariat Directorate.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年五十三。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 孝光以文章負名當世，其文一取法古人，而不趨世尚，非先秦、兩漢語，弗以措辭。

translations.literal: Xiaoguang bore a name in his age for literary composition; his writing took the ancients alone as model and did not pursue contemporary fashion—unless it was language of pre-Qin and the two Han dynasties, he would not use it in phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoguang was renowned in his day for his writing, which took the ancients as its sole model and refused to follow contemporary fashion. He would use no phrasing that did not belong to pre-Qin or Han prose.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 宇文公諒，字子貞，其先成都人，父挺祖，徙吳興，今為吳興人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Gongliang, styled Zizhen—his forebears were men of Chengdu; his father Tingzu moved to Wuxing, and he is now a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gongliang, styled Zizhen, was descended from a Chengdu family. His father Tingzu moved to Wuxing, and Gongliang was regarded as a native of that place.

sentences.zh: 公諒通經史百氏言，弱冠，有操行。

translations.literal: Gongliang was versed in the classics, histories, and the teachings of the hundred schools; at the capping age he already had conduct and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang mastered the classics, histories, and the teachings of the hundred schools, and even in early adulthood was known for his moral character.

sentences.zh: 嘉興富民延為子弟師，夜將半，聞有叩門者，問之，乃一婦人，公諒厲聲叱去之。

translations.literal: A wealthy man of Jiaxing engaged him as teacher for his sons and nephews. Near midnight he heard someone knocking at the door; asking, it proved to be a woman, and Gongliang sharply shouted and drove her away.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man in Jiaxing hired him to tutor his sons. Near midnight someone knocked at the door—it was a woman. Gongliang sharply rebuked her and sent her away.

sentences.zh: 翌日，即以他事辭歸，終不告以其故。

translations.literal: The next day he at once resigned and returned on other pretexts, and to the end never told the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he resigned on another pretext and left, never explaining what had happened.

sentences.zh: 至順四年，登進士第，授徽州路同知婺源州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Vice Administrator of Wuyuan Prefecture in Huizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhishun he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Vice Administrator of Wuyuan Prefecture in Huizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，改同知餘姚州事。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, he was transferred to Vice Administrator of Yuyao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was reassigned as Vice Administrator of Yuyao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夏不雨，公諒出禱輒應，歲以有年，民頌之，以為別駕雨。

translations.literal: In summer when rain did not fall, whenever Gongliang went out to pray, rain responded at once; the year thereby had harvest, and the people praised him, calling it the Vice-Prefect's Rain.
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought, rain fell whenever Gongliang prayed for it. The harvest was saved, and the people praised him, calling the rain "the Vice-Prefect's blessing."

sentences.zh: 攝會稽縣，申明冤滯，所活者眾。

translations.literal: Acting for Kuaiji County, he clarified wrongfully detained cases, and those he saved were many.
translations.idiomatic: While administering Kuaiji County, he cleared numerous wrongful imprisonments and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 省檄察實松江海塗田，公諒以潮汐不常，後必貽患，請一概免科，省臣從之。

translations.literal: The province issued a dispatch to inspect and verify tidal-flat fields at Songjiang. Gongliang argued that tides were inconstant and would later surely bring calamity, and requested that taxation be entirely waived; the provincial officials assented.
translations.idiomatic: When the province ordered an inspection of tidal farmland at Songjiang, Gongliang argued that the tides were unpredictable and would eventually cause disaster. He petitioned to exempt the land from taxation entirely, and the provincial authorities agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷高郵府推官，未幾，除國子助教，日與諸生辯析諸經，六館之士，資其陶甄者往往出為名臣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Judicial Officer of Gaoyou Prefecture; before long he was appointed Associate Instructor of the Imperial Academy, daily debating and analyzing the various classics with the students. Scholars of the six halls who received his molding and refinement often later emerged as famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to judicial officer at Gaoyou Prefecture, then soon appointed Associate Instructor of the Imperial Academy, where he debated the classics daily with his students. Many who passed through his instruction later became distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 調應奉翰林文字、同知制誥，兼國史院編修官，以病得告。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Document Drafting Official and Associate Director of Edicts, concurrently Compiler of the National History Institute; on account of illness he obtained leave.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin document-drafting official and Associate Director of Edicts, while also serving as compiler at the National History Institute. Illness eventually forced him to retire.

sentences.zh: 後召為國子監丞，除江浙儒學提舉，改僉嶺南廉訪司事，以疾請老。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy, appointed Commissioner for Confucian Schools in Jiangzhe, then transferred to Assistant Commissioner of the Lingnan Surveillance Commission; on account of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy, appointed Commissioner for Confucian Schools in Jiangzhe, then transferred to the Lingnan Surveillance Commission. Illness finally led him to request retirement.

sentences.zh: 公諒平居，雖暗室，必正衣冠端坐，嘗挾手記一冊，識其編首曰：「晝有所為，暮則書之，其不可書，即不敢為，天地鬼神，實聞斯言。」

translations.literal: In ordinary life Gongliang, even in a dark room, always straightened his robes and cap and sat upright. He once carried a notebook, marking at its beginning: "What one does by day, at evening one writes it down; what cannot be written, one dare not do—Heaven and Earth and the ghosts and spirits truly hear these words."
translations.idiomatic: In daily life Gongliang kept his robes straight and sat properly even in private. He carried a notebook whose opening page read: "Record each day's deeds each evening; if a deed cannot be recorded, do not do it—Heaven, Earth, and the spirits are witness to this vow."

sentences.zh: 其檢飭之嚴如此。

translations.literal: His self-discipline and restraint were strict to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the severity of his self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 所著述，有《折桂集》、《觀光集》、《辟水集》、《以齋詩稿》、《玉堂漫稿》、《越中行稿》，凡若干卷。

translations.literal: Among his writings were Collected Writings on Plucking the Cassia, Collected Writings on Viewing the Light, Collected Writings on Parting the Waters, Poems of the Yizhai Studio, Casual Drafts from the Jade Hall, and Drafts from a Journey through Yue—altogether several juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included the Collected Writings on Plucking the Cassia, Collected Writings on Viewing the Light, Collected Writings on Parting the Waters, Poems of the Yizhai Studio, Casual Drafts from the Jade Hall, and Drafts from a Journey through Yue—several works in all.

sentences.zh: 門人私諡曰純節先生。

translations.literal: His disciples privately posthumously titled him Master Chunjie.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master of Pure Integrity.

sentences.zh: 伯顏，一名師聖，字宗道，哈剌魯氏，隸軍籍蒙古萬戶府，世居開州濮陽縣。

translations.literal: Bayan, also named Shisheng, styled Zongdao, of the Karluq clan, registered in the Mongol Myriarchate military household, for generations resided in Puyang County, Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan, also called Shisheng and styled Zongdao, belonged to the Karluq clan and was registered with the Mongol Myriarchate. His family had long lived in Puyang County, Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 伯顏生三歲，常以指畫地，或三或六，若為卦者。

translations.literal: When Bayan was three years old, he often used his finger to draw on the ground, sometimes three lines or six, as if forming hexagrams.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of three Bayan would trace figures on the ground with his finger—threes and sixes, as though casting hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 六歲，從裡儒授《孝經》、《論語》，即成誦。

translations.literal: At six years he followed a local Confucian in receiving instruction in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, and at once could recite them complete.
translations.idiomatic: At six he studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects under a local scholar and could recite both from memory immediately.

sentences.zh: 蚤喪父，其兄曲出，買經傳等書以資之，日夜誦不輟。

translations.literal: He lost his father early; his elder brother, born of a concubine, bought the classics, commentaries, and other books to supply him, and day and night he recited without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was supported by his elder half-brother, who bought him classical texts and commentaries. He studied day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 稍長，受業宋進士建安黃坦，坦曰：「此子穎悟過人，非諸生可比。」

translations.literal: When he had grown somewhat, he received instruction from the Song jinshi Huang Tan of Jian'an. Tan said: "This boy's keen comprehension surpasses other men—not comparable to ordinary students."
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he studied under Huang Tan of Jian'an, a jinshi of the Song dynasty. Huang Tan said, "This boy's intelligence far surpasses ordinary students."

sentences.zh: 因命以顏為氏，且名而字之焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered that he take Yan as surname, and both named and styled him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gave him the surname Yan and chose both his given name and style.

sentences.zh: 久之，坦辭曰：「餘不能為爾師，群經有硃子說具在，歸而求之可也。」

translations.literal: After a long while Tan declined, saying: "I cannot be your teacher; among the classics Zhu Xi's explanations are fully preserved—return and seek them, and that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Huang Tan declined to teach him further, saying, "I can no longer be your teacher. Zhu Xi's commentaries on the classics are complete—go home and study them on your own."

sentences.zh: 伯顏自弱冠，即以斯文為己任，其於大經大法，粲然有睹，而心所自得，每出於言意之表。

translations.literal: From the capping age Bayan took this culture as his own charge; in the great classics and great principles he had clear sight, and what his heart attained by itself often went beyond words and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: From early adulthood Bayan devoted himself to the Confucian tradition. He grasped the great principles of the classics with luminous clarity, and insights that went beyond words arose constantly from within.

sentences.zh: 鄉之學者，來相質難，隨問隨辨，咸解其惑。

translations.literal: Scholars of the locality came to pose difficult questions; as asked, so he debated, and all had their doubts resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Local scholars came to test him with hard questions; he answered each as it came and resolved every doubt.

sentences.zh: 於是中原之士，聞而從遊者日益眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars of the Central Plains, hearing of him, daily grew more numerous in following him in study.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread across the Central Plains, and students flocked to him in ever-growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，以隱士徵至京師，授翰林待制，預修《金史》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng, summoned as a recluse he reached the capital and was appointed Hanlin Attendant Drafting Official, participating in compiling the History of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was summoned to the capital as a reclusive scholar, appointed Hanlin Attendant Drafting Official, and took part in compiling the History of Jin.

sentences.zh: 既畢，辭歸。

translations.literal: When it was finished, he resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was complete, he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 已而復起為江西廉訪僉事，數月，以病免。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised again as Assistant Commissioner of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission; after several months, on account of illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Assistant Commissioner of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission, but after a few months illness forced him to resign.

sentences.zh: 及還，四方之來學者，至千餘人。

translations.literal: When he returned, students coming from the four quarters reached more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After his return, more than a thousand students came from every direction to study with him.

sentences.zh: 蓋其為學專事講解，而務真知力踐，不屑事舉子詞章，而必期措諸實用。

translations.literal: Generally, in his pursuit of learning he devoted himself solely to explication, yet strove for true knowing and vigorous practice; he disdained pursuing examination essay composition, yet always expected application in practical use.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching focused on explication and insisted on genuine understanding put into action. He scorned the art of examination essays and demanded that learning prove itself in real life.

sentences.zh: 士出其門，不問知其為伯顏氏學者。

translations.literal: Scholars who emerged from his gate—without asking, one knew them as students of the Bayan school.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who had studied under him could be recognized at once as a disciple of the Bayan school.

sentences.zh: 至於異端之徒，亦往往棄其學而學焉。

translations.literal: As for followers of heterodox teachings, they too often abandoned their learning and studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: Even followers of heterodox schools often abandoned their old doctrines to study with him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，河南賊蔓延河北，伯顏言於省臣，將結其鄉民為什伍以自保，而賊兵大至，伯顏乃渡漳北行，邦人從之者數十萬家。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, bandits in Henan spread into Hebei. Bayan spoke to the provincial officials, intending to organize his township people into groups of ten and five for self-defense, but bandit troops arrived in force. Bayan then crossed the Zhang River and traveled north; people of the region who followed him numbered several hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year bandits from Henan swept into Hebei. Bayan urged the provincial authorities to organize local militia in groups of ten and five, but rebel forces arrived in overwhelming numbers. He crossed the Zhang River and fled north, followed by several hundred thousand local families.

sentences.zh: 至磁，與賊遇，賊知伯顏名士，生劫之以見賊將，誘以富貴，伯顏罵不屈，引頸受刃，與妻子俱死之，年六十有四。

translations.literal: Reaching Ci, he encountered bandits. Knowing Bayan was a famed scholar, they seized him alive to present him to the bandit general and tempted him with wealth and rank. Bayan cursed and would not submit, extended his neck to receive the blade, and died together with wife and children, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: At Ci he was captured by rebels who knew his reputation as a scholar. They brought him before their commander and offered wealth and rank if he would submit. Bayan cursed them and refused. He bared his neck to the blade and died together with his wife and children, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 既死，人或剖其腹，見其心數孔，曰：「古稱聖人心有七竅，此非賢士乎！」

translations.literal: After his death, someone cut open his belly and saw his heart had several openings, saying: "The ancients said the sage's heart has seven apertures—is this not a worthy man!"
translations.idiomatic: After his death someone opened his body and found several openings in his heart. "The ancients said a sage's heart has seven apertures," they exclaimed—"was this not a man of true worth?"

sentences.zh: 乃納心其腹中，覆牆而掩之。

translations.literal: They then returned the heart to his belly, covered it with a wall, and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: They replaced his heart, walled over the grave, and buried him with honor.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事，贈奉議大夫、僉太常禮儀院事，諡文節。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported the matter upward; he was posthumously granted Supporter of Discussion Grand Master and Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his death to the court, which posthumously granted him the title Supporter of Discussion Grand Master and Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with the posthumous name Wenjie, Literary Integrity.

sentences.zh: 太常諡議曰：「以城守論之，伯顏無城守之責而死，可與江州守李黼一律；

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices' posthumous-title deliberation said: "Judging by defense of cities, Bayan bore no duty to defend a city yet died—he may be classed with Li Fu, defender of Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In deliberating his posthumous title, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued: "Measured by the standard of defending a city, Bayan had no garrison duty yet died defending the people—he may be ranked with Li Fu, who held Jiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 以風紀論之，伯顏無在官之責而死，可與西台御史張桓並駕。

translations.literal: judging by integrity and discipline, Bayan bore no duty while in office yet died—he may be matched in carriage with Censor Zhang Huan of the Western Branch.
translations.idiomatic: measured by moral courage, he held no official post yet died for principle—he may stand alongside the western censor Zhang Huan.

sentences.zh: 以平生有用之學，成臨義不奪之節，乃古之所謂君子人者。」

translations.literal: With useful learning throughout his life, he achieved the integrity of not being swayed when facing righteousness—he was what the ancients called a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: A lifetime of practical learning, tested and unbroken at the moment of crisis—this was the kind of man the ancients called a true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 時以為確論。

translations.literal: At the time this was considered a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded this as the correct judgment.

sentences.zh: 伯顏平生，修輯《六經》，多所著述，皆毀於兵。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Bayan edited and compiled the Six Classics and wrote extensively, but all were destroyed in the warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan spent his life editing the Six Classics and writing extensively, but all his work was lost in the wars.

sentences.zh: 贍思，字得之，其先大食國人。

translations.literal: Zhan Si, styled Dezhi—his forebears were men of the Dashi kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Si, styled Dezhi, was descended from families of the Arab lands.

sentences.zh: 國既內附，大父魯坤，乃東遷豐州。

translations.literal: After the kingdom submitted internally, his grandfather Lukun moved east to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After their homeland submitted to the Yuan, his grandfather Lukun migrated east to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，以材授真定、濟南等路監榷課稅使，因家真定。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taizong, on account of talent he was appointed Supervisor of Tax Levies for the circuits of Zhending, Jinan, and others, and thereby made his home in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong, Lukun was appointed supervisor of tax levies for the Zhending and Jinan circuits on account of his ability, and the family settled in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 父斡直，始從儒先生問學，輕財重義，不干仕進。

translations.literal: His father Wanzhi first followed Confucian masters in seeking learning; he treated wealth lightly and valued righteousness, and did not pursue advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wanzhi studied under Confucian masters, valued integrity over wealth, and never sought official advancement.

sentences.zh: 贍思生九歲，日記古經傳至千言。

translations.literal: When Zhan Si was nine years old, each day he memorized ancient classics and commentaries to the length of a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: At nine Zhan Si could memorize a thousand characters of classical text each day.

sentences.zh: 比弱冠，以所業就正於翰林學士承旨王思廉之門，由是博極群籍，汪洋茂衍，見諸踐履，皆篤實之學，故其年雖少，已為鄉邦所推重。

translations.literal: By the capping age he brought his accomplishments for correction to the gate of Hanlin Academician Wang Silian; thereby he exhaustively mastered the multitude of books, vast and luxuriant in extension. Seen in practice, all were solid and real learning; therefore though his years were few, he was already esteemed and honored in his home region.
translations.idiomatic: By early adulthood he submitted his work to the Hanlin academician Wang Silian for correction. Thereafter he mastered an enormous range of texts and put his learning into earnest practice. Though still young, he was already highly respected in his community.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，詔以科第取士，有勸其就試者，贍思笑而不應。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou, an edict took scholars by examination ranks; some urged him to enter the examination, but Zhan Si smiled and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the court began selecting officials by examination at the start of the Yanyou era, friends urged him to compete. Zhan Si only smiled and refused.

sentences.zh: 既而侍御史郭思貞、翰林學士承旨劉賡、參知政事王士熙交章論薦之。

translations.literal: Before long Attending Censor Guo Sizhen, Hanlin Academician Liu Geng, and Vice Administrator Wang Shixi jointly submitted memorials recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the censor Guo Sizhen, Hanlin academician Liu Geng, and Vice Administrator Wang Shixi submitted joint memorials recommending him.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，詔以遺逸徵至上都，見帝於龍虎台，眷遇優渥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiding, an edict summoned him as a neglected worthy to Shangdu; he saw the emperor at Longhu Terrace and received gracious favor, generous and thick.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiding he was summoned to Shangdu as a neglected scholar of talent. Received by the emperor at Longhu Terrace, he was treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 時倒剌沙柄國，西域人多附焉，贍思獨不往見。

translations.literal: At the time Tarmashirin held the state; many men of the Western Regions attached themselves to him, but Zhan Si alone did not go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prime Minister Tarmashirin held power, and many men from the western regions sought his patronage. Zhan Si alone refused to visit him.

sentences.zh: 倒剌沙屢使人招致之，即以養親辭歸。

translations.literal: Tarmashirin repeatedly sent men to summon him, but he declined on the pretext of caring for his parents and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tarmashirin repeatedly sent envoys to summon him, but Zhan Si declined on the grounds of caring for his parents and returned home.

sentences.zh: 天曆三年，召入為應奉翰林文字，賜對奎章閣，文宗問曰：「卿有所著述否？」

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was summoned to enter as Hanlin Document Drafting Official and granted audience at the Kuizhang Pavilion. Emperor Wenzong asked: "Have you any writings?"
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianli he was summoned to the capital as a Hanlin document-drafting official and received audience in the Kuizhang Pavilion. Emperor Wenzong asked, "Have you written anything?"

sentences.zh: 明日，進所著《帝王心法》，文宗稱善。

translations.literal: The next day he presented his composition The Mind-Method of Emperors and Kings, and Wenzong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he presented his work The Mind-Method of Emperors and Kings, which Wenzong praised warmly.

sentences.zh: 詔預修《經世大典》，以論議不合求去，命奎章閣侍書學士虞集諭留之，贍思堅以母老辭，遂賜幣遣之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to participate in compiling the Great Institutions for Governing the Age; because his views did not accord he requested departure. He was ordered that Kuizhang Attendant Calligraphy Scholar Yu Ji should instruct him to remain, but Zhan Si firmly declined on the ground that his mother was old, and he was thereupon granted gifts and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to help compile the Great Institutions for Governing the Age, but disagreements led him to request leave. The emperor sent Yu Ji to persuade him to stay, but Zhan Si insisted that his mother needed care and was dismissed with gifts.

sentences.zh: 復命集傳旨曰：「卿且暫還，行召卿矣。」

translations.literal: Again he ordered Ji to transmit the imperial message: "For now return temporarily—you will soon be summoned again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent word through Yu Ji: "Return home for now—you will be summoned again soon."

sentences.zh: 至順四年，除國子博士，丁內艱，不赴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun he was appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy; upon mourning for his mother, he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhishun he was appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy, but after his mother's death he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 後至元三年，拜陝西行台監察御史，即上封事十條，曰：法祖宗，攬權綱，敦宗室，禮勳舊，惜名器，開言路，复科舉，罷數軍，一刑章，寬禁網。

translations.literal: In the third year of Houto Yuan he was appointed Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and at once submitted a sealed memorial of ten items, saying: follow the ancestral laws; gather the reins of authority; treat the imperial clan generously; honor meritorious elders; cherish titles and offices; open the path of speech; restore the examination system; abolish multiple armies; unify penal statutes; loosen the prohibition net.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Houto Yuan he was appointed censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and immediately submitted a sealed memorial with ten proposals: uphold ancestral law, centralize authority, strengthen the imperial clan, honor meritorious veterans, guard official titles, open channels for remonstrance, restore the civil service examinations, disband redundant armies, unify the penal code, and loosen harsh prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 時奸臣變亂成憲，帝方虛己以聽，贍思所言，皆一時群臣所不敢言者。

translations.literal: At the time wicked ministers altered and disrupted established statutes; the emperor was just then emptying himself to listen. What Zhan Si spoke were all things that ministers of the time dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: At a time when corrupt ministers were overturning established law and the emperor was listening with an open mind, Zhan Si spoke truths that no other official at court dared utter.

sentences.zh: 侍御史趙承慶見之，歎曰：「御史言及此，天下福也。」

translations.literal: Attending Censor Zhao Chengqing, seeing it, sighed and said: "That the censor speaks to this point is fortune for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Zhao Chengqing read the memorial and sighed, "When a censor speaks like this, it is a blessing for the empire."

sentences.zh: 戚里有執政陝西行省者，恣為非道，贍思發其罪而按之，輒棄職夜遁。

translations.literal: A kinsman by marriage who held power in the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat acted wantonly in unrighteous ways; Zhan Si exposed his crimes and investigated him, whereupon he abruptly abandoned office and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful relative who governed Shaanxi abused his authority. Zhan Si exposed his crimes and opened an investigation, and the man fled his post under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 會有詔勿逮問，然猶杖其私人。
