translations.literal: It happened that an edict came not to pursue and question him, yet still the cudgel was applied to his private retainers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then arrived forbidding further pursuit of the official himself, though his personal retainers were still flogged.

sentences.zh: 及分巡雲南，按省臣之不法者，其人即解印以去，遠籓為之震悚。

translations.literal: When he toured Yunnan on separate inspection, he investigated provincial ministers who violated the law; those men at once surrendered their seals and left, and the distant borderlands were shaken in awe.
translations.idiomatic: When he toured Yunnan as investigating censor, officials guilty of misconduct surrendered their seals and fled at once, and the distant borderlands trembled at his name.

sentences.zh: 襄、漢流民，聚居宋之紹熙府故地，至數千戶，私開鹽井，自相部署，往往劫囚徒，殺巡卒，贍思乃擒其魁，而釋其黨。

translations.literal: Wandering people from Xiang and Han gathered in the former territory of the Song's Shaoxi Prefecture, reaching several thousand households; they privately opened salt wells and deployed themselves; they often robbed prisoners and killed patrol soldiers; Zhan Si then seized their chiefs and released their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Xiang and Han had settled in the old lands of Song Shaoxi Prefecture—several thousand households who operated illegal salt wells and organized themselves, often raiding prisoners and killing patrolmen. Zhan Si arrested their leaders but released the rest.

sentences.zh: 复上言：「紹熙土饒利厚，流戶日增，若以其人散還本籍，恐為邊患，宜設官府以撫定之。」

translations.literal: He again memorialized upward, saying, "Shaoxi's soil is fertile and profits thick; wandering households increase daily; if these people are scattered back to their native registers, I fear they may become a border calamity—it is fitting to establish government offices to pacify and settle them."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Shaoxi's land is fertile and profitable, and refugee households grow daily. If we disperse them to their home registers they may become a border threat. We should establish an office to settle and govern them."

sentences.zh: 詔即其地置紹熙宣撫司。

translations.literal: An edict immediately established the Shaoxi Pacification Commission at that place.
translations.idiomatic: The court established the Shaoxi Pacification Commission on the spot.

sentences.zh: 三年，除僉浙西肅政廉訪司事，即按問都轉運鹽使、海道都萬戶、行宣政院等官贓罪，浙右郡縣，無敢為貪墨者。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Western Zhejiang Surveillance Commission; he at once investigated the Salt Transport Commissioner, the Maritime Route Commander, the Branch Commission for Buddhist Affairs, and other officials for corruption crimes; in the prefectures and counties of western Zhejiang none dared practice greed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Associate Commissioner of the Western Zhejiang Surveillance Commission and immediately investigated the Salt Transport Commissioner, the Maritime Route Commander, and officials of the Branch Commission for Buddhist Affairs for corruption. After that, no official in western Zhejiang dared enrich himself illegally.

sentences.zh: 復以浙右諸僧寺，私蔽猾民，有所謂道人、道民、行童者，類皆瀆常倫，隱徭役，使民力日耗，契勘嘉興一路，為數已二千七百，乃建議請勒歸本族，俾供王賦，庶以少寬民力。

translations.literal: He further found that in western Zhejiang the Buddhist temples privately sheltered crafty commoners—so-called Dao persons, Dao commoners, and traveling youths—who mostly violated ordinary human relations, concealed corvée labor, and caused the people's strength to be daily depleted; verifying Jiaxing Circuit alone, the number already reached 2,700; he therefore proposed requesting that they be compelled to return to their clans and made to supply the king's taxes, hoping thereby somewhat to ease the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also found that temples in western Zhejiang sheltered crafty laymen registered as Dao persons, Dao commoners, or traveling youths—men who evaded family obligations and corvée labor. In Jiaxing Circuit alone he counted 2,700 such cases. He proposed forcing them back to their clans to pay regular taxes and thus ease the burden on common people.

sentences.zh: 朝廷是之，即著以為令。

translations.literal: The court approved this and immediately enacted it as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal and promulgated it as law.

sentences.zh: 四年，改僉浙東肅政廉訪司事，以病免歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commission and resigned on grounds of illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commission, then resigned citing illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 贍思歷官台憲，所至以理冤澤物為己任，平反大辟之獄，先後甚眾，然未嘗故出人罪，以市私恩。

translations.literal: Zhan Si through his offices in the censorate, wherever he went took rectifying wrongs and benefiting things as his charge; he reversed capital cases, numerous before and after, yet never intentionally released guilty persons to trade for private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his censorial career Zhan Si made righting wrongs and helping the afflicted his duty. He reversed many capital convictions, yet never deliberately freed the guilty to win private gratitude.

sentences.zh: 嘗與五府官決獄咸寧，有婦宋娥者，與鄰人通，鄰人謂娥曰：「我將殺而夫。」

translations.literal: Once he joined the five offices in judging a case at Xianning; there was a woman Song E who had an affair with a neighbor; the neighbor said to E, "I will kill your husband."
translations.idiomatic: Once at Xianning he joined officials of the five offices to judge a case. A woman named Song E had taken a neighbor as lover. The neighbor told her, "I am going to kill your husband."

sentences.zh: 娥曰：「張子文行且殺之。」

translations.literal: E said, "Zhang Ziwen is about to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: E replied, "Zhang Ziwen is about to kill him."

sentences.zh: 明日，夫果死，跡盜數日，娥始以張子文告其姑。

translations.literal: The next day the husband indeed died; they tracked a thief for several days; only then did E tell her mother-in-law about Zhang Ziwen.
translations.idiomatic: The next day her husband was found dead. For days investigators pursued a thief. Only then did E tell her mother-in-law that Zhang Ziwen was responsible.

sentences.zh: 五府官以為非共殺，且既經赦宥，宜釋之，贍思曰：「張子文以為娥固許之矣。

translations.literal: The five-office officials held it was not joint killing, and since amnesty had already been granted, he should be released; Zhan Si said, "Zhang Ziwen believed that E had already agreed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The five offices held it was not joint murder and that amnesty had already applied, so Zhang should be released. Zhan Si said, "Zhang Ziwen acted believing E had already consented.

sentences.zh: 且娥夫死及旬，乃始言之，是娥與張同謀，度不能終隱，故發之也，豈赦可釋哉？」

translations.literal: Moreover, E's husband had been dead for ten days before she first spoke—this shows E and Zhang plotted together, judging they could not hide it forever, and therefore exposed it; how can amnesty release them?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, E waited ten days after her husband's death before speaking. She and Zhang had plotted together and, seeing they could not hide it forever, exposed the matter. How can amnesty excuse that?"

sentences.zh: 樞密判官曰：「平反活人，陰德也。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs judge said, "Reversing a case to preserve a life is hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs judge said, "To reverse a verdict and save a life is hidden virtue.

sentences.zh: 御史勿執常法。」

translations.literal: Censor, do not cling to ordinary law."
translations.idiomatic: Censor, do not cling so rigidly to the letter of the law."

sentences.zh: 贍思曰：「是謂故出人罪，非平反也。

translations.literal: Zhan Si said, "That is what is called intentionally releasing a guilty person—it is not reversing a case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Si replied, "That would be deliberately releasing the guilty—not reversing a wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 且公欲種陰德於生者，奈死者何！」

translations.literal: Moreover, if you wish to plant hidden virtue on the living, what of the dead!"
translations.idiomatic: And if you wish to store up hidden virtue for the living, what of the dead man?"

sentences.zh: 乃獨上議刑部，卒正娥罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he alone submitted opinion to the Ministry of Justice, and in the end E's guilt was confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: He alone submitted his opinion to the Ministry of Justice, and in the end Song E was convicted.

sentences.zh: 其審刑當罪多類此。

translations.literal: His judging of punishments and fitting guilt was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his judgments of guilt and punishment followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，除江東肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 十年，召為秘書少監，議治河事，皆辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat to deliberate on river control, but all were declined on grounds of illness and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat to advise on river control, but he declined both appointments citing illness.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒於家，年七十有四。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died at home, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died at home at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，皇太子撫軍冀寧，承製封拜，贈嘉議大夫、禮部尚書、上輕車都尉，追封恆山郡侯，諡曰文孝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Crown Prince pacified the army in Jining and, by imperial order for enfeoffment, posthumously granted him Grand Master for Exalted Counsel, Minister of Rites, and Chief Commandant of Light Chariots of the Upper Rank, with posthumous enfeoffment as Marquis of Hengshan Commandery and posthumous title Literary and Filial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Crown Prince, campaigning in Jining, issued an enfeoffment order posthumously granting him Grand Master for Exalted Counsel, Minister of Rites, and Chief Commandant of Light Chariots of the Upper Rank, with posthumous title Marquis of Hengshan and the posthumous epithet Literary and Filial.

sentences.zh: 贍思邃於經，而《易》學尤深，至於天文、地理、鐘律、算數、水利，旁及外國之書，皆究極之。

translations.literal: Zhan Si was profound in the classics, and in Yi learning especially deep; as for astronomy, geography, pitch pipes and regulation, calculation, and water control, extending even to books of foreign lands—all were investigated to their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Si was deeply versed in the classics, especially the Book of Changes. He also pursued astronomy, geography, music theory, mathematics, hydraulics, and even foreign texts to their limits.

sentences.zh: 家貧，饘粥或不繼，其考訂經傳，常自樂也。

translations.literal: His household was poor; gruel sometimes did not continue in succession, yet in collating and revising the classics and commentaries he was always joyful himself.
translations.idiomatic: His household was poor—sometimes he lacked even plain gruel—yet he found constant joy in collating and revising the classics.

sentences.zh: 所著述有《四書闕疑》、《五經思問》、《奇偶陰陽消息圖》、《老莊精詣》、《鎮陽風土記》、《續東陽志》、《重訂河防通議》、 《西國圖經》、《西域異人傳》、《金哀宗記》、《正大諸臣列傳》、《審聽要訣》，及文集三十卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: What he authored and wrote includes Doubts on the Four Books, Reflections on the Five Classics, Diagram of Odd and Even, Yin and Yang, and Message, Essential Reach of Laozi and Zhuangzi, Record of Feng and Soil of Zhenyang, Continued Gazetteer of Dongyang, Revised General Discussion on River Defense, Illustrated Classic of Western Lands, Biographies of Strange Men of the Western Regions, Record of the Lamenting Emperor of Jin, Biographies of Ministers of the Zhengda Era, Essentials of Careful Hearing, and a collected works in thirty juan, stored in his household.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Doubts on the Four Books, Reflections on the Five Classics, Diagram of Odd and Even, Yin and Yang, and Message, Essential Reach of Laozi and Zhuangzi, Record of Zhenyang's Local Conditions, Continued Gazetteer of Dongyang, Revised General Discussion on River Defense, Illustrated Classic of Western Lands, Biographies of Strange Men of the Western Regions, Record of the Lamenting Emperor of Jin, Biographies of Ministers of the Zhengda Era, Essentials of Careful Hearing, and a thirty-juan collected works kept at home.
